title: Efficacy and Safety of Cangrelor in Women Versus Men During Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Insights From the Cangrelor versus Standard Therapy to Achieve Optimal Management of Platelet Inhibition (CHAMPION PHOENIX) Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of a randomised trial of 11,145 patients, of whom 3051 (28%) were female.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis with non-significant interaction tests for the primary and stent thrombosis end points.
appraisal.one_line: Sex-specific analysis of cangrelor versus clopidogrel during PCI from a randomised trial.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Cangrelor reduced the odds of the primary end point by 35% in women (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 0.65; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.48-0.89) and by 14% in men (OR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.70-1.05; P interaction=0.23) compared with clopidogrel.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It supports consistent benefit of intravenous P2Y12 inhibition in women undergoing PCI, with a signal of more moderate bleeding.

title: Benefits and Risks of Extended Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Everolimus-Eluting Stents.

appraisal.design_and_n: Post hoc subset of a randomised trial; the DAPT study enrolled 25,682 subjects (11,308 EES-treated), and 9,961 (4,703 with EES) were randomized to 18 months of continued thienopyridine or placebo.
appraisal.main_limitation: Stent type was not randomized and the EES subset analysis was post hoc.
appraisal.one_line: Post hoc analysis of the DAPT study in everolimus-eluting stent patients showing fewer stent thromboses and MIs but more bleeding and death with extended thienopyridine.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Among EES-treated patients, continued thienopyridine reduced stent thrombosis (0.3% vs. 0.7%, hazard ratio [HR]: 0.38, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.15 to 0.97; p = 0.04) and MI (2.1% vs. 3.2%, HR: 0.63, 95% CI: 0.44 to 0.91; p = 0.01) versus placebo but did not reduce a composite of death, MI, and stroke (4.3% vs. 4.5%, HR: 0.89, 95% CI: 0.67 to 1.18; p = 0.42), and increased moderate/severe bleeding (2.5% vs. 1.3%, HR: 1.79, 95% CI: 1.15 to 2.80; p = 0.01), and death (2.2% vs. 1.1%, HR: 1.80, 95% CI: 1.11 to 2.92; p = 0.02).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the benefit-risk balance of prolonged DAPT with contemporary stents.

title: Six Versus 12 Months of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Implantation of Biodegradable Polymer Sirolimus-Eluting Stent: Randomized Substudy of the I-LOVE-IT 2 Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised noninferiority substudy of the I-LOVE-IT 2 trial; 1829 patients randomized to either 6-month (n=909) or 12-month DAPT (n=920).
appraisal.main_limitation: Event rates were low and the substudy is limited to one stent platform in a Chinese population.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised noninferiority substudy of 6 versus 12 months of DAPT after a biodegradable polymer sirolimus-eluting stent.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The 12-month target lesion failure in 6-month DAPT group was comparable with the 12-month DAPT group (6.8% versus 5.9%; difference and 95% confidence interval, 0.87% [-1.37% to 3.11%], P for noninferiority=0.0065).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds randomised evidence to the shortened DAPT strategies after contemporary DES.

title: Bioresorbable Coronary Scaffold Thrombosis: Multicenter Comprehensive Analysis of Clinical Presentation, Mechanisms, and Predictors.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective multicentric registry, 1,305 consecutive patients who received 1,870 BVS in 4 hospitals.
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective registry with before-and-after comparison, so the implantation effect is an association.
appraisal.one_line: Multicentre registry analysis of scaffold thrombosis after bioresorbable scaffold implantation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The incidence of probable and definite ScT was 1.8% at 30 days and 3.0% at 12 months. When a BVS-specific implantation strategy was implemented, 12-month ScT rates fell from 3.3% to 1.0% (hazard ratio: 0.19; 95% confidence interval: 0.05 to 0.70).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It quantifies scaffold thrombosis and suggests that implantation technique was associated with lower rates.

title: Is Bare-Metal Stent Implantation Still Justifiable in High Bleeding Risk Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention?: A Pre-Specified Analysis From the ZEUS Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Pre-specified analysis of a randomised single-blinded trial; 828 patients fulfilling pre-defined clinical or biochemical HBR criteria.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup of a trial using a first-generation-era zotarolimus stent and a protocol-mandated short DAPT, which limits transferability to current stents.
appraisal.one_line: Pre-specified ZEUS analysis in high-bleeding-risk patients found fewer MACE with a zotarolimus-eluting stent than with a bare-metal stent.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Among HBR patients, major adverse cardiovascular events occurred in 22.6% of the E-ZES and 29% of the BMS patients (hazard ratio: 0.75; 95% confidence interval: 0.57 to 0.98; p = 0.033), driven by lower myocardial infarction (3.5% vs. 10.4%; p < 0.001) and target vessel revascularization (5.9% vs. 11.4%; p = 0.005) rates in the E-ZES arm.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on stent choice and DAPT duration in high-bleeding-risk patients.

title: Development and Validation of a Prediction Rule for Benefit and Harm of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Beyond 1 Year After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prediction rule derived in 11,648 randomised DAPT Study patients and externally validated in 8136 patients from the PROTECT trial.
appraisal.main_limitation: Modest discrimination (c statistics of 0.70 and 0.68 in derivation, 0.64 and 0.64 in validation) and no prospective evaluation.
appraisal.one_line: Derivation and validation of a score for ischaemic and bleeding risk with DAPT continuation beyond 1 year after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Among the high score group (score ≥2, n = 5917), continued thienopyridine vs placebo was associated with reduced ischemic events (2.7% vs 5.7%; risk difference [RD], -3.0% [95% CI, -4.1% to -2.0%], P < .001) compared with the low score group (score <2, n = 5731; 1.7% vs 2.3%; RD, -0.7% [95% CI, -1.4% to 0.09%], P = .07; interaction P < .001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It offers a tool for individualising DAPT duration, a common decision.

title: Duration of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy: A Systematic Review for the 2016 ACC/AHA Guideline Focused Update on Duration of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy in Patients With Coronary Artery Disease: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Task Force on Clinical Practice Guidelines.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 randomized controlled trials that enrolled 33 051 patients receiving predominantly newer-generation DES, plus one RCT of 21 162 patients after MI.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract notes that evidence for increased mortality with prolonged DAPT comes from post hoc analyses and is weak.
appraisal.one_line: Systematic review with Bayesian and frequentist analyses supporting the 2016 ACC/AHA focused update on DAPT duration.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Use of DAPT for 12 months, as compared with use for 3 to 6 months, resulted in no significant differences in incidence of death (odds ratio [OR]: 1.17; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.85 to 1.63), major hemorrhage (OR: 1.65; 95% CI: 0.97 to 2.82), MI (OR: 0.87; 95% CI: 0.65 to 1.18), or stent thrombosis (OR: 0.87; 95% CI: 0.49 to 1.55).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It is the evidence base for the guideline position on DAPT duration after DES and after MI.

title: Duration of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy: A Systematic Review for the 2016 ACC/AHA Guideline Focused Update on Duration of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy in Patients With Coronary Artery Disease: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Task Force on Clinical Practice Guidelines.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 randomized controlled trials that enrolled 33 051 patients receiving predominantly newer-generation DES, plus one RCT of 21 162 patients after MI.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract notes that evidence for increased mortality with prolonged DAPT comes from post hoc analyses and is weak.
appraisal.one_line: Systematic review with Bayesian and frequentist analyses supporting the 2016 ACC/AHA focused update on DAPT duration.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Use of DAPT for 12 months, as compared with use for 3 to 6 months, resulted in no significant differences in incidence of death (odds ratio [OR]: 1.17; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.85 to 1.63), major hemorrhage (OR: 1.65; 95% CI: 0.97 to 2.82), MI (OR: 0.87; 95% CI: 0.65 to 1.18), or stent thrombosis (OR: 0.87; 95% CI: 0.49 to 1.55).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It is the evidence base for the guideline position on DAPT duration after DES and after MI.

title: Reduction in Ischemic Events With Ticagrelor in Diabetic Patients With Prior Myocardial Infarction in PEGASUS-TIMI 54.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Subgroup analysis of a randomised trial of 21,162 patients, including 6,806 with diabetes and 14,355 without; median follow-up 33 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis, with increased TIMI major bleeding (HR: 2.56; 95% CI: 1.52 to 4.33; p = 0.0004).
appraisal.one_line: Diabetes subgroup of a randomised trial of ticagrelor in patients with prior MI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The relative risk reduction in MACE with ticagrelor was consistent for the pooled doses versus placebo in patients with diabetes (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.84; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.72 to 0.99; p = 0.035) and without diabetes (HR: 0.84; 95% CI: 0.74 to 0.96; p = 0.013; p interaction = 0.99).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It supports long-term P2Y12 inhibition in higher-risk patients after MI, with a larger absolute effect in diabetes.

title: Deferred versus conventional stent implantation in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (DANAMI 3-DEFER): an open-label, randomised controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label randomised controlled trial at 4 Danish centres, 1215 patients (612 standard PCI, 603 deferred).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design in four centres.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of deferred versus conventional stent implantation in STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Events comprising the primary endpoint occurred in 109 (18%) patients who had standard PCI and in 105 (17%) patients who had deferred stent implantation (hazard ratio 0·99, 95% CI 0·76-1·29; p=0·92).
appraisal.why_it_matters: A neutral result for routine deferred stenting in primary PCI.

title: Early Stent Thrombosis and Mortality After Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Patient-Level Analysis of 2 Randomized Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Patient-level pooled analysis of the HORIZONS-AMI and EUROMAX randomised trials; 4935 patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention with stent implantation at 188 international sites.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc pooling of two trials with differing designs; early stent thrombosis events were few.
appraisal.one_line: Patient-level pooled analysis of two STEMI trials associating bivalirudin with more acute stent thrombosis than heparin with or without a GPI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Early ST occurred in 100 patients (2.0%), 20 of whom (20.0%) died. Bivalirudin was associated with higher rates of early ST compared with heparin±GPI (2.5% versus 1.6%, P=0.04), because of more acute (≤24 h) ST (1.5% versus 0.2%, P<0.0001), with the risk limited to the first 4 hours after percutaneous coronary intervention.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Clarifies the mechanism of the stent thrombosis signal with bivalirudin, relevant to anticoagulant choice in primary PCI.

title: Biolimus-A9 polymer-free coated stent in high bleeding risk patients with acute coronary syndrome: a Leaders Free ACS sub-study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Sub-study of a randomised trial, 659 ACS patients (BA9-DCS 330, BMS 329) from 2466 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup of a larger trial, and the comparator was a bare-metal stent rather than a current-generation DES.
appraisal.one_line: Pre-specified sub-study of high bleeding risk patients with ACS receiving a polymer-free drug-coated stent or a bare-metal stent with 1-month DAPT.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 12-month follow-up, treatment with the BA9-DCS was more effective (clinically driven target-lesion revascularization 3.9 vs. 9.0%, P = 0.009) and safer (cumulative incidence of cardiac death, myocardial infarction, or definite or probable stent thrombosis 9.3 vs. 18.5%, P = 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It informs stent choice and short DAPT in high bleeding risk patients with ACS.

title: Optimal P2Y12 Inhibitor in Patients With ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Undergoing Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Network Meta-Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Bayesian network meta-analysis of clinical trials; 37 studies with 88,402 STEMI patients and 5,077 MACE analysed.
appraisal.main_limitation: Indirect comparisons mix randomised and observational studies and may be confounded by trial era and background therapy.
appraisal.one_line: Bayesian network meta-analysis in STEMI favouring prasugrel over clopidogrel and standard ticagrelor for MACE, with both newer agents better than clopidogrel.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Outcomes at 1 month (22 studies and 60,783 patients) suggest that prasugrel was associated with: lower MACE than clopidogrel (standard dose odds ratio [OR]: 0.59, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.50 to 0.69; high-dose OR: 0.60, 95% CI: 0.51 to 0.71; upstream OR: 0.79, 95% CI: 0.66 to 0.94), and ticagrelor (standard dose OR: 0.69, 95% CI: 0.56 to 0.84; upstream OR: 0.72, 95% CI: 0.50 to 1.05).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the choice of P2Y12 inhibitor in primary PCI, where direct head-to-head randomised data were limited.

title: 6-Month Versus 12-Month Dual-Antiplatelet Therapy Following Long Everolimus-Eluting Stent Implantation: The IVUS-XPL Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial at 20 centres in Korea; 1,400 patients (mean total stent length >45 mm) randomly assigned to 6-month (n = 699) or 12-month (n = 701) DAPT.
appraisal.main_limitation: Low event rates limit power for the composite and for stent thrombosis, and the population was Korean.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of 6 versus 12 months of DAPT after long everolimus-eluting stent implantation found no increase in the composite with shorter therapy.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 15 patients (2.2%) in the 6-month DAPT group and 14 patients (2.1%) in the 12-month DAPT group (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.07; p = 0.854).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports shorter DAPT even in long-stent, higher-risk lesions, where concern about thrombosis was greatest.

title: Effect of Post-Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Bivalirudin Infusion on Acute Stent Thrombosis: Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of randomised trials: 5 trials including 16,294 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Few trials with heterogeneous infusion regimens and rare events, giving wide intervals.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis and network meta-analysis of post-PCI bivalirudin infusion dose and acute stent thrombosis in primary PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Continuing Biv-Full gave a risk ratio of 0.90, 95% confidence interval: 0.32 to 2.54; p = 0.852 for acute stent thrombosis. After 30 days, bivalirudin decreased the risk for major bleeding compared with heparin (risk ratio: 0.29; 95% confidence interval: 0.16 to 0.53; p < 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses a dosing question behind the heparin versus bivalirudin debate in STEMI.

title: Prolonged dual antiplatelet therapy in stable coronary disease: comparative observational study of benefits and harms in unselected versus trial populations.

appraisal.design_and_n: Observational cohort with trial transportability analysis; 7238 patients who survived a year or more after MI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Applies trial relative risks to observational baseline risks, assuming constant relative effects across populations.
appraisal.one_line: Estimates the benefit and harm of prolonged ticagrelor after MI in an unselected population by applying PEGASUS-TIMI-54 effects to CALIBER.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 1676/7238 (23.1%) patients met trial inclusion and exclusion criteria ("target" population).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows that absolute ischaemic benefit and bleeding harm are both higher in unselected patients than in the trial.

title: Short-versus long-term Dual Antiplatelet therapy after drug-eluting stent implantation in women versus men: A sex-specific patient-level pooled-analysis of six randomized trials.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled individual patient data from 6 randomized trials: 11,473 randomized patients, 3,454 (30%) women.
appraisal.main_limitation: Interaction tests are underpowered and the trials used different regimens and populations.
appraisal.one_line: Patient-level pooled analysis of six DAPT-duration trials testing whether sex modifies the effect of short versus long DAPT after DES.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with long-term DAPT, short-term DAPT was associated with similar rates of MACE in both women (HR 0.88; 95% CI 0.62-1.25) and men (HR 1.25; 95% CI 0.95-1.6; P interaction = 0.08).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs sex-specific DAPT duration, a population question beyond the original trials.

title: Combined Use of Bivalirudin and Radial Access in Acute Coronary Syndromes Is Not Superior to the Use of Either One Separately: Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of randomised trials: Eight trials with a total of 27,491 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Indirect subgroup comparison across trials with differing access-site mix.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis testing whether bivalirudin and radial access add bleeding benefit when combined in acute coronary syndromes.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Bivalirudin reduced major bleeding risk in patients with femoral access (OR: 0.51; 95% CI: 0.46 to 0.6; p < 0.001) but not in patients with radial access (OR: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.45 to 1.26; p = 0.28).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Questions the added value of bivalirudin when radial access is used.

title: Routine invasive versus selective invasive strategies for Non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndromes: An Updated meta-analysis of randomized trials.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of randomised trials: Twelve trials with 9,650 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Trials span eras and crossover rates, and the benefit is mainly in myocardial infarction.
appraisal.one_line: Updated meta-analysis of routine versus selective invasive strategies for non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndromes.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A routine invasive strategy was associated with a reduction in the composite of all-cause mortality or myocardial infarction (OR: 0.86, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.77-0.96). The risk of all-cause mortality was non-significantly reduced (OR: 0.88, 95% CI: 0.77-1.01).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Summarises randomised evidence behind invasive strategy in NSTE-ACS.

title: Prasugrel Versus Ticagrelor in Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction Treated With Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Multicenter Randomized PRAGUE-18 Study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 1230 patients assigned across 14 sites.
appraisal.main_limitation: Terminated early with broad confidence intervals; primary endpoint at 7 days.
appraisal.one_line: Head-to-head randomised comparison of prasugrel and ticagrelor in primary PCI for acute MI was stopped for futility and showed no difference at 7 days.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The occurrence of the primary end point did not differ between groups receiving prasugrel and ticagrelor (4.0% and 4.1%, respectively; odds ratio, 0.98; 95% confidence interval, 0.55-1.73; P=0.939).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses a common choice of P2Y12 inhibitor in STEMI, though underpowered.

title: Effective anti-thrombotic therapy without stenting: intravascular optical coherence tomography-based management in plaque erosion (the EROSION study).

appraisal.design_and_n: Single-centre uncontrolled prospective study; 60 patients enrolled and 55 completed 1-month follow-up.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-arm, single-centre, with an imaging surrogate primary endpoint and short follow-up.
appraisal.one_line: Proof-of-concept study of antithrombotic therapy without stenting for ACS caused by plaque erosion identified by OCT.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Forty-seven patients (47/60, 78.3%; 95% confidence interval: 65.8-87.9%) met the primary endpoint.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Signal for a stent-free strategy in a distinct ACS mechanism, supporting a randomised trial.

title: The EBC TWO Study (European Bifurcation Coronary TWO): A Randomized Comparison of Provisional T-Stenting Versus a Systematic 2 Stent Culotte Strategy in Large Caliber True Bifurcations.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial in 20 European centres; Two hundred patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small sample and 12-month follow-up limit power for a composite of clinical events.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised comparison of provisional T-stenting with a systematic culotte strategy in large-calibre true bifurcation lesions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point (a composite of death, myocardial infarction, and target vessel revascularization at 12 months) occurred in 7.7% of the provisional T-stent group versus 10.3% of the culotte group (hazard ratio, 1.02; 95% confidence interval, 0.78-1.34; P=0.53).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It tests the consensus view that complex bifurcations with large side branches need an upfront two-stent technique, and the simpler strategy did not differ on the composite.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Complex PCI.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled patient-level analysis of 6 randomised trials; 9,577 patients, 1,680 (17.5%) with complex PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis across trials not designed for the question; the complexity definition was post hoc.
appraisal.one_line: Pooled analysis of six DAPT-duration trials suggested long-term DAPT reduced MACE after complex PCI but not after non-complex PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with short-term DAPT, long-term DAPT yielded significant reductions in MACE in the complex PCI group (adjusted HR: 0.56; 95% CI: 0.35 to 0.89) versus the noncomplex PCI group (adjusted HR: 1.01; 95% CI: 0.75 to 1.35; pinteraction = 0.01).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests whether procedural complexity should guide DAPT duration.

title: Bivalirudin or unfractionated heparin in patients with acute coronary syndromes managed invasively with and without ST elevation (MATRIX): randomised controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised open-label trial, 7213 patients with ACS (4010 with and 3203 without ST elevation).
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis of a trial whose overall results were published previously.
appraisal.one_line: Prespecified analysis by ST-elevation status found no benefit of bivalirudin over heparin on MACE or net adverse events in ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In patients with ST segment elevation, major adverse cardiovascular events occurred in 118 (5.9%) assigned to bivalirudin and 129 (6.5%) assigned to heparin (rate ratio 0.90, 95% confidence interval 0.70 to 1.16; P=0.43)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs anticoagulant choice during invasive ACS management.

title: Prevention of Bleeding in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation Undergoing PCI.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised three-arm trial, 2124 participants.
appraisal.main_limitation: Not powered for efficacy; broad confidence intervals for ischaemic outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial in atrial fibrillation after PCI found less clinically significant bleeding with rivaroxaban-based regimens than with a vitamin K antagonist plus DAPT.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: hazard ratio for group 1 vs. group 3, 0.59; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.47 to 0.76; P<0.001; hazard ratio for group 2 vs. group 3, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.50 to 0.80; P<0.001
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs antithrombotic regimen choice in a common PCI population.

title: Three, six, or twelve months of dual antiplatelet therapy after DES implantation in patients with or without acute coronary syndromes: an individual patient data pairwise and network meta-analysis of six randomized trials and 11 473 patients.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient data pairwise and network meta-analysis of six trials; 11 473 randomized patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Trials used aspirin plus clopidogrel and enrolled relatively low-risk ACS patients.
appraisal.one_line: Patient-level pairwise and network meta-analysis of DAPT duration found the optimal duration differed by clinical presentation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In ACS patients, ≤6-month DAPT was associated with non-significantly higher 1-year rates of MI or ST compared with 1-year DAPT (Hazard Ratio (HR) 1.48, 95% Confidence interval (CI) 0.98-2.22; P = 0.059)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs DAPT duration by presentation.

title: Clinical Outcome of Double Kissing Crush Versus Provisional Stenting of Coronary Artery Bifurcation Lesions: The 5-Year Follow-Up Results From a Randomized and Multicenter DKCRUSH-II Study (Randomized Study on Double Kissing Crush Technique Versus Provisional Stenting Technique for Coronary Artery Bifurcation Lesions).

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; A total of 370 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single technique comparison with a borderline primary result and subgroup analysis by lesion complexity.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year follow-up of the DKCRUSH-II trial comparing double kissing crush with provisional stenting in bifurcation lesions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 5 years, the major adverse cardiac event rate (23.8%) in the provisional stenting group was insignificantly different to that of the double kissing group (15.7%; P=0.051). Target lesion revascularization was 16.2% versus 8.6% (P=0.027).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Long-term data on two-stent techniques in complex bifurcations inform strategy choice.

title: Clinically significant bleeding with low-dose rivaroxaban versus aspirin, in addition to P2Y12 inhibition, in acute coronary syndromes (GEMINI-ACS-1): a double-blind, multicentre, randomised trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Double-blind randomised trial, 3037 patients with acute coronary syndromes.
appraisal.main_limitation: Safety-focused and not powered for efficacy.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of low-dose rivaroxaban in place of aspirin plus a P2Y12 inhibitor after ACS found similar clinically significant bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: TIMI non-CABG clinically significant bleeding was similar with rivaroxaban versus aspirin therapy (total 154 patients [5%]; 80 participants [5%] of 1519 vs 74 participants [5%] of 1518; HR 1·09 [95% CI 0·80-1·50]; p=0·5840).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests an aspirin-free dual-pathway approach in ACS.

title: Personalising the decision for prolonged dual antiplatelet therapy: development, validation and potential impact of prognostic models for cardiovascular events and bleeding in myocardial infarction survivors.

appraisal.design_and_n: Electronic health record cohort (CALIBER, England), development n = 12 694 and validation n = 5613 patients one year after acute myocardial infarction.
appraisal.main_limitation: Benefit and harm estimates apply trial effect sizes to observational risk and the models were not tested prospectively.
appraisal.one_line: Prognostic models for ischaemic and bleeding events at one year after MI were developed to personalise prolonged DAPT.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Models for cardiovascular events (c-index: 0.75 (95% CI: 0.74, 0.77)) and bleeding (c index 0.72 (95% CI: 0.67, 0.77)) were well calibrated; there was a net clinical benefit of prolonged DAPT in 63-99% patients depending on how benefits and harms were weighted.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Individualised risk-benefit estimation addresses a common decision on DAPT duration after MI where trials give average effects only.

title: Subclinical leaflet thrombosis in surgical and transcatheter bioprosthetic aortic valves: an observational study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled observational analysis of two registries (RESOLVE and SAVORY), 931 patients had CT imaging and 890 had interpretable scans.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised antithrombotic allocation with CT at varying intervals after implantation.
appraisal.one_line: Subclinical leaflet thrombosis on CT was more frequent after TAVR than SAVR and was less frequent with anticoagulation than with DAPT.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 106 (12%) of 890 patients had subclinical leaflet thrombosis, including five (4%) of 138 with thrombosis of surgical valves versus 101 (13%) of 752 with thrombosis of transcatheter valves (p=0·001); thrombosis was less frequent with anticoagulants (eight [4%] of 224) than with dual antiplatelet therapy (31 [15%] of 208; p<0·0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs antithrombotic choice after bioprosthetic aortic valve implantation and the leaflet thrombosis debate.

title: Bleeding-Related Deaths in Relation to the Duration of Dual-Antiplatelet Therapy After Coronary Stenting.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of RCTs; individual patient data for 6 RCTs and aggregate data for 12 RCTs.
appraisal.main_limitation: Attribution of death to bleeding relied on timing within 1 year of a bleeding episode, and the link between bleeding and death is observational.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis with individual patient data linking bleeding, mortality and DAPT duration after drug-eluting stent implantation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Bleeding was an independent predictor of mortality within 1 year of the bleeding episode (hazard ratio: 6.93; 95% confidence interval: 4.53 to 10.60; p < 0.0001). Shorter DAPT was associated with lower rates of bleeding-related deaths compared with prolonged DAPT (hazard ratio: 0.65; 95% confidence interval: 0.43 to 0.99; p = 0.04).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It offers a mechanistic account of why shorter DAPT has been associated with lower all-cause mortality in trials of DAPT duration.

title: Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Continuation Beyond 1 Year After Drug-Eluting Stents: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of four trials comprising 17 650 participants.
appraisal.main_limitation: Few trials with differing stent types and drugs, and trial-level data only.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of randomised trials of DAPT continued beyond one year after drug-eluting stents, using frequentist and Bayesian methods.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Extended DAPT did not affect all-cause mortality (odds ratio [OR], 1.11; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.79-1.5; P=0.53), was associated with a reduction in the risk of myocardial infarction (OR, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.43-0.73; P<0.001) and an increased risk of major bleeding (OR, 1.49; 95% CI, 1.06-2.11; P=0.02).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Summarises the ischaemic benefit and bleeding cost of prolonged DAPT that underpins duration decisions.

title: Benefit of switching dual antiplatelet therapy after acute coronary syndrome: the TOPIC (timing of platelet inhibition after acute coronary syndrome) randomized study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label, monocentric, randomized trial; Six hundred and forty six patients were randomized and 645 analysed (322 switched DAPT, 323 unchanged DAPT); 1-year follow-up.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-centre open-label design with a composite endpoint that includes BARC 2 or higher bleeding.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of switching from a newer P2Y12 blocker to clopidogrel one month after ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 43 (13.4%) patients in the switched DAPT group and in 85 (26.3%) patients in the unchanged DAPT (HR 95%CI 0.48 (0.34-0.68), P < 0.01).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It supports de-escalation of DAPT after the early phase of ACS, although a larger multicentre confirmation is needed.

title: Aspirin Versus Aspirin Plus Clopidogrel as Antithrombotic Treatment Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement With a Balloon-Expandable Valve: The ARTE (Aspirin Versus Aspirin + Clopidogrel Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised controlled trial of 222 patients, 111 allocated to DAPT and 111 to SAPT, stopped after inclusion of 74% of the planned population.
appraisal.main_limitation: Underpowered and stopped early, with no effect estimate and confidence interval for the primary endpoint.
appraisal.one_line: Small randomised trial of aspirin alone versus aspirin plus clopidogrel after balloon-expandable TAVR, stopped early.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The composite of death, MI, stroke or transient ischemic attack, or major or life-threatening bleeding tended to occur more frequently in the DAPT group (15.3% vs. 7.2%, p = 0.065). DAPT was associated with a higher rate of major or life-threatening bleeding events (10.8% vs. 3.6% in the SAPT group, p = 0.038).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds randomised evidence that single antiplatelet therapy is a reasonable default after TAVR, with less bleeding.

title: Dual Antiplatelet Therapy for 6 Versus 18 Months After Biodegradable Polymer Drug-Eluting Stent Implantation.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised trial of 3,773 patients; intention-to-treat analysis in 3,307 patients followed for at least 6 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design, wide noninferiority margin and a low event rate.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised noninferiority trial of 6 versus 18 months of DAPT after a biodegradable polymer drug-eluting stent.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: NACCE occurred in 34 patients (2.1%) receiving short-term DAPT and 24 patients (1.5%) receiving long-term DAPT (difference 0.6%, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.5 to 0.3). Noninferiority of short-term DAPT was confirmed.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds randomised evidence on shortened DAPT duration after a contemporary DES, relevant to strategy decisions.

title: 6- Versus 24-Month Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Implantation of Drug-Eluting Stents in Patients Nonresistant to Aspirin: Final Results of the ITALIC Trial (Is There a Life for DES After Discontinuation of Clopidogrel).

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised trial in which 926 were randomized to 6-month and 924 to 24-month DAPT.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, underpowered for individual components, and restricted to aspirin-sensitive patients.
appraisal.one_line: Two-year results of the ITALIC randomised trial comparing 6 with 24 months of DAPT after second-generation drug-eluting stents.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 2 years, the composite endpoint was unchanged, at 3.5% for 6 months and 3.7% for 24 months (p = 0.79). There was a trend toward higher mortality with longer DAPT (2.2% vs. 1.2%; p = 0.11).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports short DAPT after contemporary DES with no ischaemic penalty over two years.

title: Outcome of percutaneous coronary intervention with the Absorb bioresorbable scaffold: data from the Swedish Coronary Angiography and Angioplasty Registry (SCAAR).
journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort from the Swedish Coronary Angiography and Angioplasty Registry: Absorb BRS (n=810) compared with modern DES (n=67,909), mean follow-up two years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational comparison with residual confounding, and non-compliance with DAPT guidelines was noted.
appraisal.one_line: Nationwide registry comparison of the Absorb scaffold with modern drug-eluting stents, showing higher definite stent thrombosis with the scaffold.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The Absorb BRS was associated with a higher crude incidence of definite ST at stent level: 1.5 vs. 0.6%, hazard ratio (HR) 2.38 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.34-4.23), adjusted HR 4.34 (95% CI: 2.37-7.94); p<0.001.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Confirms in unselected national practice the late thrombosis signal seen in randomised trials of the scaffold.

title: Comparative efficacy and safety of reperfusion therapy with fibrinolytic agents in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials; 40 eligible studies involving 128 071 patients treated with 12 different fibrinolytic regimens; PROSPERO CRD42016042131.
appraisal.main_limitation: Indirect comparisons across trials of different eras and background therapy.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis of fibrinolytic regimens for STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with accelerated infusion of alteplase with parenteral anticoagulants as background therapy, streptokinase and non-accelerated infusion of alteplase were significantly associated with an increased risk of all-cause mortality (risk ratio [RR] 1·14 [95% CI 1·05-1·24] for streptokinase plus parenteral anticoagulants; RR 1·26 [1·10-1·45] for non-accelerated alteplase plus parenteral anticoagulants).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It ranks fibrinolytic regimens for settings where primary PCI is not available, where the choice of agent affects mortality and bleeding.

title: Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection: Clinical Outcomes and Risk of Recurrence.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective single-centre cohort (Vancouver General Hospital), 327 SCAD patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-centre observational study with no randomised evidence on medical therapy.
appraisal.one_line: A large prospective SCAD cohort showed frequent long-term events, with hypertension and absence of beta-blocker use associated with recurrence.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Median long-term follow-up was 3.1 years, and overall major adverse cardiac event rate was 19.9%; recurrent SCAD occurred in 10.4% of patients; hypertension increased (hazard ratio: 2.46; p = 0.011) and beta-blocker use diminished (hazard ratio: 0.36; p = 0.004) recurrent SCAD.
appraisal.why_it_matters: SCAD management is guided by observational data only, so these findings shape secondary prevention practice.

title: Risk of Early Adverse Events After Clopidogrel Discontinuation in Patients Undergoing Short-Term Dual Antiplatelet Therapy: An Individual Participant Data Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual participant data analysis of 11,473 PCI patients from 6 randomized trials, plus an aggregate meta-analysis of 11 trials including 38,919 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Few early events limit precision, and trials differed in design and stent type.
appraisal.one_line: Individual participant data analysis testing for a rebound of ischaemic events after clopidogrel discontinuation following short-term DAPT.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: During the first 90 days following clopidogrel discontinuation, there was no significant increase in the risk of MACCE between patients randomized to short-term DAPT compared with long-term DAPT (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.18; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.71 to 1.98; p = 0.52).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses safety of DAPT de-escalation by showing no early rebound after stopping clopidogrel at 3 or 6 months.

title: Dual Antithrombotic Therapy with Dabigatran after PCI in Atrial Fibrillation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised trial; 2725 patients with atrial fibrillation who had undergone PCI; mean follow-up 14 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design, with the noninferiority margin for thromboembolic events and the sample size leaving wide uncertainty for individual ischaemic events.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial showing that dual therapy with dabigatran and a P2Y12 inhibitor caused less bleeding than warfarin-based triple therapy after PCI in atrial fibrillation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The incidence of the primary end point was 15.4% in the 110-mg dual-therapy group as compared with 26.9% in the triple-therapy group (hazard ratio, 0.52; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.42 to 0.63; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P<0.001 for superiority) and 20.2% in the 150-mg dual-therapy group as compared with 25.7% in the corresponding triple-therapy group, which did not include elderly patients outside the United States (hazard ratio, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.88; P<0.001 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It addresses the antithrombotic regimen after PCI in a large, common population and supports removing aspirin early to reduce bleeding.

title: Bivalirudin versus Heparin Monotherapy in Myocardial Infarction.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicenter, randomized, registry-based, open-label clinical trial; 6006 patients (3005 STEMI and 3001 NSTEMI).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design with 180-day follow-up.
appraisal.one_line: Registry-based randomised comparison of bivalirudin and heparin monotherapy during PCI for myocardial infarction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 180 days, a primary end-point event had occurred in 12.3% of the patients (369 of 3004) in the bivalirudin group and in 12.8% (383 of 3002) in the heparin group (hazard ratio, 0.96; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.83 to 1.10; P=0.54).
appraisal.why_it_matters: In a contemporary radial-access, potent-P2Y12 setting, bivalirudin offered no advantage over heparin alone, which simplifies anticoagulation choice in MI.

title: Guided de-escalation of antiplatelet treatment in patients with acute coronary syndrome undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (TROPICAL-ACS): a randomised, open-label, multicentre trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Investigator-initiated, randomised, open-label, assessor-blinded, multicentre trial at 33 sites; 2610 patients (1304 guided de-escalation, 1306 control); 1-year follow-up.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design, non-inferiority margin of 30%, and the strategy combines early de-escalation with platelet function testing so the contribution of each is not separable.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of platelet function test guided de-escalation from prasugrel to clopidogrel after ACS treated with PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 95 patients (7%) in the guided de-escalation group and in 118 patients (9%) in the control group (pnon-inferiority=0·0004; hazard ratio [HR] 0·81 [95% CI 0·62-1·06], psuperiority=0·12).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It supports early de-escalation of potent P2Y12 inhibition as an alternative after ACS, a common decision on which guidelines are cautious.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Ticagrelor Over Time in Patients With Prior MI in PEGASUS-TIMI 54.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified landmark analysis of a randomized trial; 21,162 patients randomized and followed for 33 months (median).
appraisal.main_limitation: Secondary landmark analysis, with wide confidence intervals at individual landmarks.
appraisal.one_line: Landmark analysis of the effect and bleeding risk of ticagrelor over time in patients with prior myocardial infarction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The benefit of ticagrelor 60 mg was consistent at each subsequent landmark (year 1 hazard ratio [HR]: 0.82; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.67 to 0.99; year 2 HR: 0.90; 95% CI: 0.74 to 1.11; and year 3 HR: 0.79; 95% CI: 0.62 to 1.00).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It shows persistent ischaemic risk years after MI and a consistent effect of low-dose ticagrelor, informing decisions on prolonged P2Y12 inhibition.

title: Timing of Angiography and Outcomes in High-Risk Patients With Non-ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction Managed Invasively: Insights From the TAO Trial (Treatment of Acute Coronary Syndrome With Otamixaban).

appraisal.design_and_n: Post hoc analysis of a randomized trial; angiography performed in 4071 patients (<12 hours, n=1648; 12-24 hours, n=1420; ≥24 hours, n=1003); 180-day outcomes.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc, non-randomised comparison of timing groups, with confounding by indication.
appraisal.one_line: Post hoc analysis of timing of angiography in high-risk NSTEMI with a GRACE score above 140.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: CAG <12 hours was associated with a lower risk of death and myocardial infarction (odds ratio, 0.71; 95% confidence interval, 0.55-0.91). Performing CAG <12 hours was also associated with a lower risk of death and myocardial infarction (odds ratio, 0.76; 95% confidence interval, 0.61-0.94; P=0.01) compared with CAG performed at 12 to 24 hours.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It bears on whether angiography within 12 hours rather than 24 hours should be pursued in high-risk NSTEMI, a question that randomised data have not settled.

title: Report of an ESC-EAPCI Task Force on the evaluation and use of bioresorbable scaffolds for percutaneous coronary intervention: executive summary.
journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Task Force report (executive summary); no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Executive summary only, and the recommendation reflects data on a single scaffold with published randomised results.
appraisal.one_line: ESC-EAPCI Task Force executive summary advising that bioresorbable scaffolds should not be preferred to conventional DES and setting a framework for evaluating new scaffolds.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets the European device-evaluation standard and a clinical position on scaffolds.

title: Differences in relative and absolute effectiveness of oral P2Y 12 inhibition in men and women: a meta-analysis and modelling study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of nine randomised trials combined with Scottish population data on 17 842 women and 27 818 men admitted with myocardial infarction.
appraisal.main_limitation: Women-specific estimate is derived by combining interaction and male effects rather than observed directly.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis and modelling study of sex-specific effects of newer P2Y12 inhibitors in ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Combined treatment RR in women for major adverse cardiovascular events 0.86 (95% CI 0.72 to 1.04); sex-treatment interaction RR 1.08 (95% CI 0.98 to 1.19).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses whether the absolute benefit of ticagrelor and prasugrel differs by sex, given higher baseline mortality in women.

title: Impact of design of coronary stents and length of dual antiplatelet therapies on ischaemic and bleeding events: a network meta-analysis of 64 randomized controlled trials and 102 735 patients.

appraisal.design_and_n: Network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials; Sixty-four studies with 150 arms and 102 735 patients; median follow-up of 20 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: Indirect comparison across trials with different designs, and the stent-by-DAPT arms are not randomised factorial comparisons.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis of stent type and DAPT duration in randomised trials.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: After a median follow-up of 20 months, MACE rates were similar in the different arms of interest. The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It maps ischaemic and bleeding outcomes jointly across stent platforms and DAPT durations, relevant to choices about device and therapy length.

title: Clinical outcomes of state-of-the-art percutaneous coronary revascularization in patients with de novo three vessel disease: 1-year results of the SYNTAX II study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicenter, all-comers, open-label, single arm study in 22 centres; 708 patients screened and discussed within the heart team, 454 deemed appropriate for PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised comparison with a historical cohort, so differences may reflect era and selection, and follow-up is 1 year.
appraisal.one_line: Single-arm multicentre study of a contemporary PCI strategy in three-vessel disease, compared with a predefined cohort from the earlier SYNTAX-I trial.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At one year, the SYNTAX-II strategy was superior to the equipoise-derived SYNTAX-I PCI cohort (MACCE SYNTAX-II 10.6% vs. SYNTAX-I 17.4%; HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.39-0.85, P = 0.006).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It tests whether physiology, imaging and device advances change PCI outcomes in three-vessel disease and supports a randomised comparison with contemporary bypass surgery.

title: Lesion Complexity and Outcomes of Extended Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of a randomized trial; enrolled n = 25,416 and randomized n = 11,554 subjects; 30 months versus 12 months of DAPT.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis of a trial of thienopyridines, with the DAPT score finding exploratory.
appraisal.one_line: Analysis of whether anatomically complex target lesions modify the effect of extended DAPT after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Reduction of MI or stent thrombosis with continued thienopyridine beyond 12 months versus placebo was similar for subjects with (2.5% vs. 4.5%; hazard ratio: 0.55; 95% confidence interval: 0.38 to 0.79; p = 0.001) and without (2.0% vs. 3.8%; hazard ratio: 0.52; 95% confidence interval: 0.39 to 0.69; p < 0.001) anatomic complexity (pinteraction = 0.81).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Lesion complexity did not modify the effect of extended DAPT, which bears on whether anatomy should guide DAPT duration.

title: International Expert Consensus on Switching Platelet P2Y12 Receptor-Inhibiting Therapies.

appraisal.design_and_n: Expert consensus document; no sample size applies.
appraisal.main_limitation: Recommendations draw on pharmacodynamic data and limited clinical outcome evidence, as the abstract notes that guidelines have not elaborated on switching.
appraisal.one_line: International expert consensus on switching between oral and intravenous P2Y12 inhibitors.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It gives guidance on a frequent clinical event, switching P2Y12 inhibitor, that guidelines have not addressed in detail.

title: Drug-eluting stents in elderly patients with coronary artery disease (SENIOR): a randomised single-blind trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised single-blind trial at 44 centres in nine countries; 1200 patients (596 DES, 604 BMS); 1-year follow-up.
appraisal.main_limitation: Industry-funded, patients were masked but operators were not, and the trial was not powered for individual components such as stent thrombosis or bleeding.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of drug-eluting versus bare-metal stents with short DAPT in patients aged 75 years or older.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 68 (12%) patients in the DES group and 98 (16%) in the BMS group (relative risk [RR] 0·71 [95% CI 0·52-0·94]; p=0·02).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It addresses a population under-represented in stent trials and supports a drug-eluting stent with short DAPT over a bare-metal stent in older patients.

title: Multisite Investigation of Outcomes With Implementation of CYP2C19 Genotype-Guided Antiplatelet Therapy After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.

appraisal.design_and_n: Non-randomised multicentre implementation study of 1,815 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised comparison with inverse probability weighting and residual confounding.
appraisal.one_line: Pragmatic multisite study of CYP2C19 genotype-guided antiplatelet therapy after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Adjusted hazard ratio: 2.26; 95% confidence interval: 1.18 to 4.32 for loss-of-function carriers on clopidogrel versus alternative therapy.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds real-world outcome data on genotype-guided de-escalation and escalation.

title: Safety of six-month dual antiplatelet therapy after second-generation drug-eluting stent implantation: OPTIMA-C Randomised Clinical Trial and OCT Substudy.
journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised multicentre trial of 1,368 patients, 684 per arm.
appraisal.main_limitation: Low event rate and modest sample size limit power for stent thrombosis.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised non-inferiority trial of six versus 12 months of DAPT after second-generation DES.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: MACE 1.2% versus 0.6% (risk difference 0.6%; 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.4-1.6%; p=0.24), non-inferiority met against 4% margin.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Contributes to the evidence on DAPT shortening after contemporary DES.

title: Rivaroxaban with or without aspirin in patients with stable coronary artery disease: an international, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial; 24 824 patients with stable coronary artery disease from 558 centres.
appraisal.main_limitation: Report of a coronary subpopulation from a larger trial, industry-funded, and limited to patients after a 30-day run-in.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of low-dose rivaroxaban with or without aspirin against aspirin alone in stable coronary artery disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The combination of rivaroxaban plus aspirin reduced the primary outcome more than aspirin alone (347 [4%] of 8313 vs 460 [6%] of 8261; hazard ratio [HR] 0·74, 95% CI 0·65-0·86, p<0·0001). Combined rivaroxaban plus aspirin treatment resulted in more major bleeds than treatment with aspirin alone (263 [3%] of 8313 vs 158 [2%] of 8261; HR 1·66, 95% CI 1·37-2·03, p<0·0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It tests dual-pathway inhibition in a large population of patients with coronary disease, many of whom have undergone PCI, with a trade-off between fewer vascular events and more bleeding.

title: 1-Year Outcomes of Patients Undergoing Primary Angioplasty for Myocardial Infarction Treated With Prasugrel Versus Ticagrelor.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomized trial; 1,230 patients with acute myocardial infarction treated with primary percutaneous coronary intervention.
appraisal.main_limitation: Switching to clopidogrel was not randomised, so the finding on switching is observational and open to confounding.
appraisal.one_line: One-year follow-up of a randomised comparison of prasugrel and ticagrelor in primary PCI for myocardial infarction, including an analysis of economically motivated switching to clopidogrel.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The endpoint occurred in 6.6% of prasugrel patients and in 5.7% of ticagrelor patients (hazard ratio: 1.167; 95% confidence interval: 0.742 to 1.835; p = 0.503).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Prasugrel and ticagrelor had similar efficacy and bleeding at 1 year, and the switch analysis informs de-escalation in practice.

title: Benefit of Switching Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Acute Coronary Syndrome According to On-Treatment Platelet Reactivity: The TOPIC-VASP Pre-Specified Analysis of the TOPIC Randomized Study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Pre-specified analysis of a randomised study including 645 patients, 305 (47%) classified as low on-treatment platelet reactivity.
appraisal.main_limitation: Substudy of a modest trial with a platelet reactivity stratification that was not the randomised factor.
appraisal.one_line: Pre-specified TOPIC substudy relating platelet reactivity to benefit of switching to aspirin and clopidogrel after ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Patients defined as LTPR and randomized to unchanged DAPT were at the highest risk of primary endpoint occurrence (31%; p < 0.01).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Relevant to guided de-escalation of DAPT after ACS.

title: Impact of Clopidogrel Therapy on Mortality and Cancer in Patients With Cardiovascular and Cerebrovascular Disease: A Patient-Level Meta-Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Patient-level meta-analysis of 6 randomized trials including 48 817 randomized patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Trials differ in populations and clopidogrel duration comparators.
appraisal.one_line: Patient-level meta-analysis finding no difference in mortality or cancer with prolonged clopidogrel.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All-cause mortality 7.23% versus 7.26%; P=0.97 for prolonged versus no or short-duration clopidogrel.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses safety concerns about extended clopidogrel using individual patient data.

title: Ticagrelor for Secondary Prevention of Atherothrombotic Events in Patients With Multivessel Coronary Disease.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified subgroup analysis of a randomised trial (PEGASUS-TIMI 54); 12,558 patients (59.4%) had MVD.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis of a single trial, with a bleeding excess in the ticagrelor arm.
appraisal.one_line: Prespecified PEGASUS-TIMI 54 analysis of ticagrelor versus placebo according to the presence of multivessel coronary disease after prior MI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In patients with MVD, ticagrelor reduced the risk of MACE (7.94% vs. 9.37%, HR: 0.82; p = 0.004) and coronary events (6.02% vs. 7.67%, HR: 0.76; p < 0.0001), including a 36% reduction in coronary death (HR: 0.64; 95% confidence interval: 0.48 to 0.85; p = 0.002).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs selection of patients for prolonged ticagrelor after MI by identifying a higher-risk group with larger absolute benefit.

title: Randomized Comparisons of Double-Dose Clopidogrel or Adjunctive Cilostazol Versus Standard Dual Antiplatelet in Patients With High Posttreatment Platelet Reactivity: Results of the CREATIVE Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Single-center, randomized, controlled trial; 1078 patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-centre design with platelet-function-guided selection; the double-dose comparison did not reach significance.
appraisal.one_line: Single-centre randomised trial of intensified antiplatelet regimens in PCI patients with high on-clopidogrel platelet reactivity by thromboelastography.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred in 52 patients (14.4%) in the STANDARD group, 38 patients (10.6%) in the DOUBLE group, and 30 patients (8.5%) in the TRIPLE group (hazard ratio, 0.720; 95% confidence interval, 0.474-1.094, DOUBLE versus STANDARD; hazard ratio, 0.550; 95% confidence interval, 0.349-0.866, TRIPLE versus STANDARD).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests whether escalating therapy in high on-treatment reactivity improves outcomes, a question left open by earlier guided-therapy trials.

title: Compliance With Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy in Contemporary Coronary Revascularization Trials.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials; 5 trials included from a total of 439 references.
appraisal.main_limitation: Only a small number of trials; meta-regression is hypothesis-generating.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis showing that compliance with guideline-directed medical therapy in PCI versus CABG trials is low and differs by arm.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Overall, compliance with GDMT1 was low and decreased over time from 67% at 1 year to 53% at 5 years.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Differential medical therapy between arms may bias PCI versus CABG comparisons.

title: Anticoagulant Use Among Patients With End-Stage Renal Disease Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: An Analysis From the National Cardiovascular Data Registry.

appraisal.design_and_n: CathPCI Registry analysis of n=71 675 patients with end-stage renal disease receiving bivalirudin or UFH.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry data with confounding by indication and in-hospital outcomes only.
appraisal.one_line: Registry analysis associating bivalirudin with lower bleeding and mortality than heparin in dialysis-dependent PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In hospital bleeding (7.0% versus 9.5%; adjusted odds ratio,0.82; 95% confidence interval, 0.76-0.87) lower with bivalirudin.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides data in a population largely excluded from antithrombotic trials.

title: Association of different antiplatelet therapies with mortality after primary percutaneous coronary intervention.

appraisal.design_and_n: BCIS national database analysis of >89 000 patients undergoing primary PCI for STEMI between 2007 and 2014.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised comparison of P2Y12 inhibitors with residual confounding.
appraisal.one_line: National registry analysis comparing prasugrel, ticagrelor and clopidogrel mortality after primary PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Prasugrel versus clopidogrel mortality at 30 days OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.78 to 0.97, P=0.014; ticagrelor versus clopidogrel at 30 days OR 1.07, 95% CI 0.95 to 1.21, P=0.237.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large real-world comparison of newer P2Y12 inhibitors in STEMI.

title: Impact of anticoagulation therapy on valve haemodynamic deterioration following transcatheter aortic valve replacement.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre study of 2466 patients with propensity matching of 622 patients per group.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational design with haemodynamic rather than clinical endpoint; few received direct oral anticoagulants.
appraisal.one_line: Multicentre cohort associating anticoagulation after TAVR with less valve haemodynamic deterioration.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: VHD was significantly lower in the AC group (0.6%) compared with the non-AC group (3.7%, P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Relevant to antithrombotic therapy after TAVR and durability.

title: Short-Term Versus Long-Term Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Drug-Eluting Stent Implantation in Elderly Patients: A Meta-Analysis of Individual Participant Data From 6 Randomized Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual participant data meta-analysis of 6 randomized trials; 5,319 elderly patients (≥65 years).
appraisal.main_limitation: Age subgroup analysis with only 12-month outcomes and trials differing in design.
appraisal.one_line: Individual participant data meta-analysis of short versus long DAPT after DES in older patients.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary outcome overall hazard ratio [HR]: 1.12; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.88 to 1.43; p = 0.3581; age interaction p for interaction = 0.0384.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs DAPT duration in older patients using patient-level data.

title: Comparison of Reduced-Dose Prasugrel and Standard-Dose Clopidogrel in Elderly Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes Undergoing Early Percutaneous Revascularization.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicenter, randomized, open-label, blinded end point trial; 1443 patients enrolled.
appraisal.main_limitation: Premature termination for futility limits precision on bleeding and stent thrombosis.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised comparison of reduced-dose prasugrel and clopidogrel in patients older than 74 years with ACS undergoing PCI, stopped early for futility.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred in 121 patients (17%) with prasugrel and 121 (16.6%) with clopidogrel (hazard ratio, 1.007; 95% confidence interval, 0.78-1.30; P=0.955).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs antiplatelet choice in older patients, a group excluded from the pivotal prasugrel trials.

title: The efficacy of early versus delayed P2Y12 inhibition in percutaneous coronary intervention for ST-elevation myocardial infarction: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of seven randomised controlled trials including 9,648 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Short follow-up and heterogeneous agents and timing.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of randomised trials of early versus delayed P2Y12 inhibition in STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: MACE OR 0.73, 95% CI: 0.61-0.88, p=0.0008; major bleeding OR 0.87, 95% CI: 0.62-1.21, p=0.41 with early inhibition.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses the timing of P2Y12 loading before primary PCI.

title: Comparison of single versus dual antiplatelet therapy after TAVR: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of six studies (3 RCTs and 3 observational studies, n = 840).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small total sample with mixed randomised and observational designs.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis associating dual antiplatelet therapy after TAVR with more bleeding than single therapy.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Major or life-threatening bleeding RR = 2.52 (95% CI 1.62-3.92, P < 0.0001) with DAPT versus SAPT.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports single antiplatelet therapy after TAVR.

title: A Multidisciplinary Approach on the Perioperative Antithrombotic Management of Patients With Coronary Stents Undergoing Surgery: Surgery After Stenting 2.

appraisal.design_and_n: Consensus document without a stated sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Expert recommendations rather than trial evidence.
appraisal.one_line: Multidisciplinary update on perioperative antithrombotic management after coronary stenting.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides practical risk-stratified guidance for surgery after stenting.

title: Pharmacogenomic Approach to Selecting Antiplatelet Therapy in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes: The PHARMCLO Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomized trial; 888 patients enrolled before premature stopping.
appraisal.main_limitation: Early termination and unequal drug use between arms may inflate the effect and limit interpretation.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of genotype-guided versus standard selection of P2Y12 inhibitor in ACS, stopped early.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 71 patients (15.9%) in the pharmacogenomic arm and in 114 (25.9%) in the standard-of-care arm (hazard ratio: 0.58; 95% confidence interval: 0.43 to 0.78; p < 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Genotype-guided antiplatelet therapy is a live guideline question and this is one of few outcome trials.

title: 6-month versus 12-month or longer dual antiplatelet therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with acute coronary syndrome (SMART-DATE): a randomised, open-label, non-inferiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised, open-label, non-inferiority trial at 31 centres in South Korea; 2712 patients randomly assigned.
appraisal.main_limitation: Wide non-inferiority margin and more myocardial infarction with short DAPT.
appraisal.one_line: Non-inferiority trial of 6-month versus 12-month or longer DAPT after PCI for ACS; the authors do not conclude short DAPT is safe.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 63 patients in the 6-month DAPT group and in 56 patients in the 12-month or longer DAPT group (cumulative event rate 4·7% vs 4·2%; absolute risk difference 0·5%; upper limit of one-sided 95% CI 1·8%; pnon-inferiority=0·03 with a predefined non-inferiority margin of 2·0%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to DAPT duration after ACS, where short-course strategies are being adopted.

title: Safety and efficacy of dual vs. triple antithrombotic therapy in patients with atrial fibrillation following percutaneous coronary intervention: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and Bayesian meta-analysis of randomised trials; 4 trials including 5317 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Few trials, heterogeneous regimens, and trials underpowered for ischaemic events.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of dual versus triple antithrombotic therapy in atrial fibrillation patients after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with the TAT arm, Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) major or minor bleeding showed a reduction by 47% in the DAT arm [4.3% vs. 9.0%; hazard ratio (HR) 0.53, 95% credible interval (CrI) 0.36-0.85, I2 = 42.9%].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports de-escalation of antithrombotic therapy in a common high-bleeding-risk group.

title: Length of stay following percutaneous coronary intervention: An expert consensus document update from the society for cardiovascular angiography and interventions.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

appraisal.design_and_n: Expert consensus document without a stated sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Expert consensus relying on selected-patient studies of early discharge.
appraisal.one_line: SCAI expert consensus update on length of stay after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Updates recommendations on same-day and early discharge after PCI.

title: A randomized multicentre trial to compare revascularization with optimal medical therapy for the treatment of chronic total coronary occlusions.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective randomized, multicentre, open-label, controlled clinical trial; Three hundred and ninety-six patients were enrolled.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design with a symptom endpoint; not powered for hard outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of PCI versus optimal medical therapy for chronic total occlusion with health status as the primary endpoint.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 12 months, a greater improvement of SAQ subscales was observed with PCI as compared with OMT for angina frequency [5.23, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.75; 8.71; P = 0.003], and quality of life (6.62, 95% CI 1.78-11.46; P = 0.007).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Few randomised data exist for CTO PCI, and this supports symptomatic benefit.

title: Device-Related Thrombus After Left Atrial Appendage Closure: Incidence, Predictors, and Outcomes.

appraisal.design_and_n: Device arms of 4 prospective FDA trials (PROTECT-AF n=463; PREVAIL n=269; CAP n=566; CAP2 n=578); 1739 patients with an implant (7159 patient-years follow-up).
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational association within trial and registry cohorts; most events occurred without detected device-related thrombus.
appraisal.one_line: Pooled analysis of Watchman trials and registries on device-related thrombus and subsequent thromboembolism.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: DRT was seen in 65 patients (3.74%). The rates of SSE with and without DRT were 7.46 and 1.78 per 100 patient-years (adjusted rate ratio, 3.55; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.18-5.79; P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large pooled estimate of device-related thrombus incidence and its link to stroke, relevant to post-implant antithrombotic therapy.

title: Five-Year Outcomes with PCI Guided by Fractional Flow Reserve.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 888 patients underwent randomization (447 in the PCI group and 441 in the medical-therapy group).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label; the difference was driven by urgent revascularisation, with no difference in death.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year follow-up of FFR-guided PCI versus medical therapy in stable coronary disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 5 years, the rate of the primary end point was lower in the PCI group than in the medical-therapy group (13.9% vs. 27.0%; hazard ratio, 0.46; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.34 to 0.63; P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Long-term physiology-guided evidence that informs revascularisation choices in chronic coronary syndromes.

title: Dabigatran in patients with myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery (MANAGE): an international, randomised, placebo-controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: International, randomised, placebo-controlled trial at 84 hospitals in 19 countries; 1754 patients randomly assigned.
appraisal.main_limitation: High treatment discontinuation and a composite endpoint with modest event numbers.
appraisal.one_line: Placebo-controlled trial of dabigatran in patients with myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The composite primary efficacy outcome occurred in fewer patients randomised to dabigatran than placebo (97 [11%] of 877 patients assigned to dabigatran vs 133 [15%] of 877 patients assigned to placebo; hazard ratio [HR] 0·72, 95% CI 0·55-0·93; p=0·0115).
appraisal.why_it_matters: First randomised evidence for treating MINS, a common and under-addressed form of myocardial injury.

title: Long-Term Mortality and Early Valve Dysfunction According to Anticoagulation Use: The FRANCE TAVI Registry.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: FRANCE TAVI registry; 12,804 patients included, 11,469 analysed for mortality and 2,555 eligible for BVD assessment.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational data with confounding by indication and missing data handled by imputation.
appraisal.one_line: FRANCE TAVI registry analysis of anticoagulation, mortality and bioprosthesis valve dysfunction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Anticoagulation at discharge (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 0.54; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.35 to 0.82; p = 0.005) and a nonfemoral approach (aOR: 0.53; 95% CI: 0.28 to 1.02; p = 0.049) were independently associated with lower rates of BVD.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Contributes to the debate on antithrombotic therapy after TAVI, where randomised data remain limited.

title: Radial versus femoral access and bivalirudin versus unfractionated heparin in invasively managed patients with acute coronary syndrome (MATRIX): final 1-year results of a multicentre, randomised controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Programme of three nested, randomised, multicentre, open-label, superiority trials; 8404 patients randomly assigned to radial or femoral access.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design with several nested randomisations.
appraisal.one_line: Final 1-year results of the MATRIX programme comparing radial versus femoral access and bivalirudin versus heparin in ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 year, major adverse cardiovascular events did not differ between patients assigned to radial access compared with those assigned to femoral access (14·2% vs 15·7%; rate ratio 0·89, 95% CI 0·80-1·00; p=0·0526), but net adverse clinical events were fewer with radial than with femoral access (15·2% vs 17·2%; 0·87, 0·78-0·97; p=0·0128).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large trial data supporting radial access and informing anticoagulant choice in ACS.

title: Ticagrelor plus aspirin for 1 month, followed by ticagrelor monotherapy for 23 months vs aspirin plus clopidogrel or ticagrelor for 12 months, followed by aspirin monotherapy for 12 months after implantation of a drug-eluting stent: a multicentre, open-label, randomised superiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised, open-label superiority trial at 130 sites in 18 countries; 15 968 participants randomly assigned.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design with an unconventional primary endpoint and a superiority hypothesis that was not met.
appraisal.one_line: Trial of one month of ticagrelor plus aspirin followed by ticagrelor monotherapy versus standard DAPT after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 2 years, 304 (3·81%) participants in the experimental group had died or had a non-fatal centrally adjudicated new Q-wave myocardial infarction, compared with 349 (4·37%) participants in the control group (rate ratio 0·87 [95% CI 0·75-1·01]; p=0·073]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Largest trial of P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy after short DAPT; shapes de-escalation debate.

title: Drug-coated balloons for small coronary artery disease (BASKET-SMALL 2): an open-label randomised non-inferiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre, open-label, randomised non-inferiority trial; 758 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label; modest sample size and a wide absolute non-inferiority margin.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised non-inferiority trial of drug-coated balloon versus DES for small-vessel coronary disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: After 12 months, the proportions of MACE were similar in both groups of the full-analysis population (MACE was 7·5% for the DCB group vs 7·3% for the DES group; hazard ratio [HR] 0·97 [95% CI 0·58-1·64], p=0·9180).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports DCB as an alternative to DES in small vessels.

title: Relations between implementation of new treatments and improved outcomes in patients with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction during the last 20 years: experiences from SWEDEHEART registry 1995 to 2014.

appraisal.design_and_n: Nationwide SWEDEHEART registry cohort of 205 693 NSTEMI cases between 1995 and 2014.
