appraisal.main_limitation: Observational temporal analysis; attribution to treatments is by statistical adjustment.
appraisal.one_line: Swedish registry analysis linking 20 years of improved NSTEMI outcomes to uptake of invasive treatment and medications.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The standardized 1-year mortality ratio compared with a control population decreased from 5.53 [95% confidence interval (CI) 5.30-5.75] to 3.03 (95% CI 2.89-3.19).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Quantifies the population-level association between guideline treatments and NSTEMI outcomes.

title: Six months versus 12 months dual antiplatelet therapy after drug-eluting stent implantation in ST-elevation myocardial infarction (DAPT-STEMI): randomised, multicentre, non-inferiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective, randomised, multicentre, non-inferiority trial; 870 randomised.
appraisal.main_limitation: Randomised after six event-free months, and the trial was small.
appraisal.one_line: Non-inferiority trial of 6 versus 12 months of DAPT after DES in STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 4.8% of patients receiving SAPT versus 6.6% of patients receiving DAPT (hazard ratio 0.73, 95% confidence interval 0.41 to 1.27, P=0.26).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Short DAPT duration after STEMI is a common practical decision.

title: Antithrombotic Therapy in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation Treated With Oral Anticoagulation Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A North American Perspective-2018 Update.

appraisal.design_and_n: Expert consensus focused update; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Consensus-derived recommendations from a regional expert group rather than a formal guideline process.
appraisal.one_line: North American focused update recommends non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants over vitamin K antagonists and double therapy by discharge for most patients with atrial fibrillation undergoing PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets expert guidance on antithrombotic regimens after PCI in anticoagulated patients, a common decision with ongoing evidence generation.

title: Open-Label Randomized Trial Comparing Oral Anticoagulation With and Without Single Antiplatelet Therapy in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and Stable Coronary Artery Disease Beyond 1 Year After Coronary Stent Implantation.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label noninferiority randomised trial (NCT01962545); 696 patients enrolled of 2000 planned.
appraisal.main_limitation: Premature termination left the trial underpowered and inconclusive, as the authors state.
appraisal.one_line: Open-label trial of oral anticoagulation alone versus with single antiplatelet therapy beyond 1 year after stenting in atrial fibrillation did not establish noninferiority and was terminated early.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred in 54 patients (15.7%) in the OAC-alone group and in 47 patients (13.6%) in the combined group (hazard ratio, 1.16; 95% CI, 0.79-1.72; P=0.20 for noninferiority, P=0.45 for superiority). Major bleeding occurred in 27 (7.8%) and 36 (10.4%) patients, respectively.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses whether antiplatelet therapy can be stopped in anticoagulated patients with stable disease after stenting, where randomised data were lacking.

title: Effect of Medication Co-payment Vouchers on P2Y12 Inhibitor Use and Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events Among Patients With Myocardial Infarction: The ARTEMIS Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Cluster randomised clinical trial (ARTEMIS, NCT02406677); 301 hospitals, 11 001 patients enrolled.
appraisal.main_limitation: Persistence was patient-reported and the effect on adherence was modest.
appraisal.one_line: Cluster randomised trial found co-payment vouchers increased P2Y12 inhibitor persistence after myocardial infarction without reducing MACE at one year.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Patient-reported persistence at 1 year was higher with vouchers (unadjusted rates, 5340/6135 [87.0%] vs 3324/3967 [83.8%], respectively; P < .001; adjusted odds ratio, 1.19 [95% CI, 1.02 to 1.40]). MACE did not differ (unadjusted cumulative incidence, 10.2% vs 10.6%; P = .65; adjusted hazard ratio, 1.07 [95% CI, 0.93 to 1.25]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests a health-system intervention on antiplatelet adherence with hard outcomes in a general-tier journal.

title: Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Duration Based on Ischemic and Bleeding Risks After Coronary Stenting.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled analysis of 8 randomised trials; 14,963 patients, 3,118 underwent complex PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis across heterogeneous trials with non-randomised stratification by risk.
appraisal.one_line: Pooled trial analysis suggests benefit of long-term DAPT after complex PCI only when high bleeding risk features are absent.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Long-term DAPT in non-HBR patients reduced ischemic events in both complex (absolute risk difference: -3.86%; 95% confidence interval: -7.71 to +0.06) and noncomplex PCI strata (absolute risk difference: -1.14%; 95% confidence interval: -2.26 to -0.02), but not among HBR patients.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs DAPT duration by weighing ischaemic and bleeding risk, a frequent decision.

title: Antithrombotic Therapy after Acute Coronary Syndrome or PCI in Atrial Fibrillation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: International two-by-two factorial randomised trial (AUGUSTUS, NCT02415400); 4614 patients from 33 countries.
appraisal.main_limitation: Not powered for ischaemic outcomes, and the apixaban comparison was open-label.
appraisal.one_line: Apixaban without aspirin caused less bleeding and fewer hospitalisations than vitamin K antagonist or aspirin-containing regimens in atrial fibrillation after ACS or PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding was noted in 10.5% of the patients receiving apixaban, as compared with 14.7% of those receiving a vitamin K antagonist (hazard ratio, 0.69; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.58 to 0.81; P<0.001 for both noninferiority and superiority), and in 16.1% of the patients receiving aspirin, as compared with 9.0% of those receiving placebo (hazard ratio, 1.89; 95% CI, 1.59 to 2.24; P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Directly informs the preferred antithrombotic regimen after PCI in anticoagulated patients, a common clinical problem.

title: Ticagrelor Versus Clopidogrel in Patients With STEMI Treated With Fibrinolysis: TREAT Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: International open-label randomised trial with blinded adjudication (TREAT, NCT02298088); 3,799 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design and exclusion of patients aged 75 years or older.
appraisal.one_line: Ticagrelor did not significantly reduce cardiovascular events compared with clopidogrel after fibrinolysis for STEMI in patients younger than 75 years.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The combined outcome occurred in 129 of 1,913 patients (6.7%) receiving ticagrelor and in 137 of 1,886 patients (7.3%) receiving clopidogrel (hazard ratio: 0.93; 95% confidence interval: 0.73 to 1.18; p = 0.53). The rates of major, fatal, and intracranial bleeding were similar.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs P2Y12 inhibitor choice in patients receiving fibrinolysis, where evidence was limited.

title: Defining high bleeding risk in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: a consensus document from the Academic Research Consortium for High Bleeding Risk.

appraisal.design_and_n: Consensus document from a 31-member consortium; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Definition derived from consensus and available evidence rather than prospective validation.
appraisal.one_line: ARC-HBR consensus document proposes a standard definition of high bleeding risk in patients undergoing PCI for trials and clinical decisions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides a common definition for trial design, regulatory review and antithrombotic decisions in high bleeding risk patients.

title: Drug-coated balloon for treatment of de-novo coronary artery lesions in patients with high bleeding risk (DEBUT): a single-blind, randomised, non-inferiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Single-blind randomised non-inferiority trial (DEBUT, NCT01781546) at five sites in Finland; 220 patients recruited, 208 assigned, drug-coated balloon (n=102) or bare metal stent (n=106).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small trial in five Finnish centres with a bare-metal stent comparator rather than a contemporary drug-eluting stent.
appraisal.one_line: Drug-coated balloon PCI was associated with fewer MACE than bare-metal stents at 9 months in high bleeding risk patients in a small single-blind trial.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 9 months, major adverse cardiac events had occurred in one patient (1%) in the drug-coated balloon group and in 15 patients (14%) in the bare-metal stent group (absolute risk difference -13·2 percentage points [95% CI -6·2 to -21·1], risk ratio 0·07 [95% CI 0·01 to 0·52]; p<0·00001 for non-inferiority and p=0·00034 for superiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests a stent-free strategy in high bleeding risk patients, a population where short antiplatelet duration is desirable.

title: Association Between Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement and Early Postprocedural Stroke.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective cohort of 101 430 patients treated at 521 US hospitals in the STS/ACC TVT Registry.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry; antithrombotic comparisons are open to confounding.
appraisal.one_line: TVT Registry analysis of early stroke after TAVR showing stable rates over time.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At day 30, there were 2290 patients (2.3%) with a stroke of any kind (95% CI, 2.2%-2.4%), and 373 patients (0.4%) with transient ischemic attacks (95% CI, 0.3%-0.4%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Defines the benchmark for periprocedural stroke that embolic protection and antithrombotic strategies must beat.

title: Effect of 1-Month Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Followed by Clopidogrel vs 12-Month Dual Antiplatelet Therapy on Cardiovascular and Bleeding Events in Patients Receiving PCI: The STOPDAPT-2 Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre open-label randomised trial (STOPDAPT-2) at 90 hospitals in Japan; 3045 patients randomised, 1-month DAPT (n=1523) or 12-month DAPT (n=1522).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label trial in a Japanese population with a composite that combines ischaemic and bleeding events.
appraisal.one_line: One month of DAPT followed by clopidogrel monotherapy was noninferior and superior to 12 months of DAPT for a composite of cardiovascular and bleeding events after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred in 2.36% with 1-month DAPT and 3.70% with 12-month DAPT (absolute difference, -1.34% [95% CI, -2.57% to -0.11%]; hazard ratio [HR], 0.64 [95% CI, 0.42-0.98]), meeting criteria for noninferiority (P < .001) and for superiority (P = .04).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds to the evidence for very short DAPT after PCI, a decision made in most stented patients.

title: Effect of P2Y12 Inhibitor Monotherapy vs Dual Antiplatelet Therapy on Cardiovascular Events in Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: The SMART-CHOICE Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label noninferiority randomised trial (SMART-CHOICE) at 33 hospitals in Korea; 2993 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design and protocol adherence of 79.3% in the monotherapy group.
appraisal.one_line: P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy after 3 months of DAPT was noninferior to 12 months of DAPT for MACCE and reduced bleeding after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 12 months, major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events occurred in 42 patients in the P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy group and in 36 patients in the DAPT group (2.9% vs 2.5%; difference, 0.4% [1-sided 95% CI, -∞% to 1.3%]; P = .007 for noninferiority). The rate of bleeding was significantly lower in the P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy group than in the DAPT group (2.0% vs 3.4%; HR, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.36-0.92; P = .02).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy after short DAPT as a de-escalation strategy.

title: Duration of dual antiplatelet therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stent: systematic review and network meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised trials; 17 studies (n=46 864).
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial-level pooling across heterogeneous populations and regimens, with short-term DAPT largely clopidogrel-based.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis found long-term DAPT increased major bleeding and non-cardiac death versus short-term DAPT, with similar efficacy of short and standard DAPT in ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with short term DAPT, long term DAPT resulted in higher rates of major bleeding (odds ratio 1.78, 95% confidence interval 1.27 to 2.49) and non-cardiac death (1.63, 1.03 to 2.59); standard term DAPT was associated with higher rates of any bleeding (1.39, 1.01 to 1.92).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Summarises DAPT duration evidence in a general-tier journal, though newer trials were accumulating.

title: Antithrombotic Therapy for Atrial Fibrillation with Stable Coronary Disease.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre open-label randomised trial in Japan (AFIRE, NCT02642419); 2236 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design, early termination, and an exclusively Japanese population on a Japanese-specific rivaroxaban dose.
appraisal.one_line: Rivaroxaban monotherapy was noninferior for efficacy and superior for major bleeding compared with rivaroxaban plus an antiplatelet in atrial fibrillation with stable coronary disease, and the trial stopped early for mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Rivaroxaban monotherapy was noninferior to combination therapy for the primary efficacy end point, with event rates of 4.14% and 5.75% per patient-year, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.72; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.55 to 0.95; P<0.001 for noninferiority). Major bleeding rates were 1.62% and 2.76% per patient-year (hazard ratio, 0.59; 95% CI, 0.39 to 0.89; P = 0.01 for superiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports omitting antiplatelet therapy in anticoagulated patients with chronic coronary disease.

title: Complete Revascularization with Multivessel PCI for Myocardial Infarction.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial (COMPLETE, NCT01740479); 2016 patients in the complete-revascularisation group and 2025 in the culprit-lesion-only group.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design, and angiographic rather than physiology-guided selection of nonculprit lesions.
appraisal.one_line: Complete revascularisation with nonculprit PCI reduced cardiovascular death or myocardial infarction compared with culprit-lesion-only PCI in STEMI with multivessel disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At a median follow-up of 3 years, the first coprimary outcome had occurred in 158 of the 2016 patients (7.8%) in the complete-revascularization group as compared with 213 of the 2025 patients (10.5%) in the culprit-lesion-only PCI group (hazard ratio, 0.74; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.60 to 0.91; P = 0.004).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Likely to change guideline recommendations on nonculprit revascularisation in STEMI, a very common decision.

title: Ticagrelor or Prasugrel in Patients with Acute Coronary Syndromes.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre open-label randomised trial (ISAR-REACT 5, NCT01944800); 4018 patients randomised.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design with unmasked treatment strategy differences, such as pretreatment, which may affect the comparison.
appraisal.one_line: Prasugrel reduced the composite of death, myocardial infarction or stroke compared with ticagrelor at one year in ACS patients undergoing planned invasive evaluation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary end-point event occurred in 184 of 2012 patients (9.3%) in the ticagrelor group and in 137 of 2006 patients (6.9%) in the prasugrel group (hazard ratio, 1.36; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.09 to 1.70; P = 0.006). Major bleeding was observed in 5.4% versus 4.8% (hazard ratio, 1.12; 95% CI, 0.83 to 1.51; P = 0.46).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Directly compares the two potent P2Y12 inhibitors in ACS and bears on guideline preference between them.

title: A Genotype-Guided Strategy for Oral P2Y12 Inhibitors in Primary PCI.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised, open-label, assessor-blinded trial; 2488 patients (1242 genotype-guided, 1246 standard).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design and a noninferiority margin of 2 percentage points; the bleeding result is a co-primary with a borderline P value.
appraisal.one_line: POPular Genetics found CYP2C19 genotype-guided P2Y12 inhibitor choice noninferior to ticagrelor or prasugrel after primary PCI, with less bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary combined outcome occurred in 63 patients (5.1%) in the genotype-guided group and in 73 patients (5.9%) in the standard-treatment group (absolute difference, -0.7 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -2.0 to 0.7; P<0.001 for noninferiority). The primary bleeding outcome occurred in 122 patients (9.8%) in the genotype-guided group and in 156 patients (12.5%) in the standard-treatment group (hazard ratio, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.61 to 0.98; P = 0.04).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports guided de-escalation of P2Y12 inhibitor therapy in STEMI, relevant to the guideline position on guided therapy.

title: Ticagrelor in patients with diabetes and stable coronary artery disease with a history of previous percutaneous coronary intervention (THEMIS-PCI): a phase 3, placebo-controlled, randomised trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified subgroup of the randomised, double-blind THEMIS trial; 11 154 patients with previous PCI, median follow-up 3·3 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: A subgroup analysis of a trial that was neutral in its overall population on net benefit terms, with a manufacturer-funded design.
appraisal.one_line: THEMIS-PCI reported that ticagrelor added to aspirin reduced cardiovascular death, MI or stroke but increased TIMI major bleeding in patients with diabetes and previous PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Fewer patients receiving ticagrelor had a primary efficacy outcome event than in the placebo group (404 [7·3%] of 5558 vs 480 [8·6%] of 5596; HR 0·85 [95% CI 0·74-0·97], p=0·013). TIMI major bleeding occurred in 111 (2·0%) of 5536 patients receiving ticagrelor and 62 (1·1%) of 5564 patients receiving placebo (HR 2·03 [95% CI 1·48-2·76], p<0·0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Defines a long-term antiplatelet option for high-ischaemic-risk patients with diabetes after PCI, with an explicit bleeding cost.

title: Edoxaban-based versus vitamin K antagonist-based antithrombotic regimen after successful coronary stenting in patients with atrial fibrillation (ENTRUST-AF PCI): a randomised, open-label, phase 3b trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised, open-label noninferiority phase 3b trial; 1506 patients (751 edoxaban, 755 VKA).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, not powered for ischaemic events, and the comparator included aspirin for 1 to 12 months.
appraisal.one_line: ENTRUST-AF PCI showed an edoxaban-based regimen was noninferior to a VKA-based regimen for major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding after PCI in atrial fibrillation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Major or CRNM bleeding events occurred in 128 (17%) of 751 patients (annualised event rate 20·7%) with the edoxaban regimen and 152 (20%) of 755 patients (annualised event rate 25·6%) patients with the VKA regimen; hazard ratio 0·83 (95% CI 0·65-1·05; p=0·0010 for non-inferiority, margin hazard ratio 1·20; p=0·1154 for superiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds a fourth DOAC-based dual therapy trial for patients with AF undergoing PCI.

title: Clinically Significant Bleeding With Ticagrelor Versus Clopidogrel in Korean Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes Intended for Invasive Management: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised trial, 800 Korean patients (400 per arm), 12-month follow-up.
appraisal.main_limitation: Underpowered for ischaemic efficacy, as the authors state.
appraisal.one_line: Korean RCT found more clinically significant bleeding with ticagrelor than clopidogrel in ACS patients intended for early invasive management.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 12 months, the incidence of clinically significant bleeding was significantly higher in the ticagrelor group than in the clopidogrel group (11.7% [45/400] vs 5.3% [21/400]; hazard ratio [HR], 2.26; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.34 to 3.79; P=0.002). The incidence of death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, or stroke was not significantly different between the ticagrelor group and the clopidogrel group (9.2% [36/400] vs 5.8% [23/400]; HR, 1.62; 95% CI, 0.96 to 2.74; P=0.07).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds a new signal for ethnicity-specific antiplatelet selection in East Asian ACS patients.

title: Ticagrelor with or without Aspirin in High-Risk Patients after PCI.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Double-blind randomised trial; 9006 enrolled, 7119 randomised after 3 months of ticagrelor plus aspirin.
appraisal.main_limitation: Event-free selection at 3 months and an ischaemic endpoint with a noninferiority margin of 1.6 percentage points; manufacturer-funded.
appraisal.one_line: TWILIGHT found ticagrelor monotherapy after 3 months of DAPT reduced clinically relevant bleeding without more death, MI or stroke in high-risk PCI patients.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The incidence of the primary end point was 4.0% among patients randomly assigned to receive ticagrelor plus placebo and 7.1% among patients assigned to receive ticagrelor plus aspirin (hazard ratio, 0.56; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.45 to 0.68; P<0.001). The incidence of death from any cause, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke was 3.9% in both groups (difference, -0.06 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.97 to 0.84; hazard ratio, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.78 to 1.25; P<0.001 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: A blinded trial of aspirin-free P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy in high-risk patients, directly shaping DAPT de-escalation recommendations.

title: Antithrombotic Therapy in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and Acute Coronary Syndrome Treated Medically or With Percutaneous Coronary Intervention or Undergoing Elective Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Insights From the AUGUSTUS Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified subgroup analysis of a 2x2 factorial randomised trial; 4614 patients (1097 medically treated ACS, 1714 ACS with PCI, 1784 elective PCI).
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis in a trial not powered for ischaemic events within each stratum.
appraisal.one_line: Prespecified AUGUSTUS analysis showed apixaban without aspirin gave less bleeding than VKA-based regimens across medically managed ACS, ACS with PCI and elective PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Apixaban compared with vitamin K antagonist reduced ISTH major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding in patients with ACS treated medically (hazard ratio [HR], 0.44 [95% CI, 0.28-0.68]), patients with ACS treated with PCI (HR, 0.68 [95% CI, 0.52-0.89]), and patients undergoing elective PCI (HR, 0.82 [95% CI, 0.64-1.04]; Pinteraction=0.052).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Extends the evidence for aspirin-free dual therapy with a DOAC to medically managed ACS.

title: High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin and the Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified secondary analysis of a stepped-wedge cluster-randomised trial, 48 282 consecutive patients with suspected ACS.
appraisal.main_limitation: Secondary analysis comparing diagnostic categories rather than a randomised comparison of treatments.
appraisal.one_line: High-STEACS secondary analysis found that implementing hs-cTn and the Universal Definition increased diagnoses of type 2 MI and myocardial injury without changes in investigation, treatment or outcomes.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Implementation increased the diagnosis of type 1 myocardial infarction by 11% (510/4471), type 2 myocardial infarction by 22% (205/916), and acute and chronic myocardial injury by 36% (443/1233) and 43% (389/898), respectively. Despite modest increases in antiplatelet therapy and coronary revascularization after implementation in patients with type 1 myocardial infarction, the primary outcome was unchanged (cause specific HR 1.00 [95% CI, 0.82-1.21]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Documents the unmet treatment need in type 2 MI and myocardial injury and motivates trials of management in those groups.

title: Sex-Specific Thresholds of High-Sensitivity Troponin in Patients With Suspected Acute Coronary Syndrome.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Stepped-wedge cluster-randomised trial across 10 hospitals; 48,282 patients (47% women).
appraisal.main_limitation: Sex-specific analysis of a diagnostic implementation trial, not a treatment trial.
appraisal.one_line: High-STEACS analysis of sex-specific hs-cTnI thresholds found more women identified with myocardial injury but unchanged outcomes and less treatment than men.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Use of the high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I assay with sex-specific thresholds increased myocardial injury in women by 42% and in men by 6%. The primary outcome occurred in 18% (369 of 2,072) and 17% (488 of 2,919) of women with myocardial injury before and after implementation, respectively (adjusted hazard ratio: 1.11; 95% confidence interval: 0.92 to 1.33).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows an under-treatment gap in women with myocardial injury that is a target for sex-specific research.

title: Safety and efficacy outcomes of double vs. triple antithrombotic therapy in patients with atrial fibrillation following percutaneous coronary intervention: a systematic review and meta-analysis of non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulant-based randomized clinical trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 4 RCTs, 10 234 patients (DAT = 5496 vs. TAT = 4738).
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial-level pooling with substantial heterogeneity in bleeding (I2 = 69%) and few stent thrombosis events.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of four NOAC-based RCTs found double therapy lowered bleeding but raised stent thrombosis versus triple therapy in AF patients undergoing PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary safety endpoint (ISTH major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding) was significantly lower with DAT compared with TAT [risk ratio (RR) 0.66, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.56-0.78; P < 0.0001; I2 = 69%]. This benefit was counterbalanced by a significant increase of stent thrombosis (RR 1.59, 95% CI 1.01-2.50; P = 0.04; I2 = 0%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Summarises the efficacy-safety trade-off of dual versus triple therapy that underlies current guideline recommendations.

title: Ticagrelor Alone Versus Dual Antiplatelet Therapy From 1 Month After Drug-Eluting Coronary Stenting.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified ancillary study of the GLOBAL LEADERS randomised trial; independent adjudication of 7,585 patients from 20 sites.
appraisal.main_limitation: Substudy of a subset of sites in an open-label trial, with the parent trial missing its primary endpoint.
appraisal.one_line: GLASSY adjudication sub-study found ticagrelor monotherapy after 1 month DAPT noninferior but not superior to conventional DAPT for ischaemic events.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The 2-year coprimary efficacy endpoint occurred in 271 (7.14%) and in 319 (8.41%) patients in the experimental and conventional groups, respectively (rate ratio [RR]: 0.85; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.72 to 0.99), fulfilling noninferiority (p noninferiority <0.001), but not superiority (p superiority = 0.0465). The rates of BARC 3 or 5 bleeding did not differ (RR: 1.00; 95% CI: 0.75 to 1.33; p = 0.986).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the contested evidence on short DAPT followed by P2Y12 monotherapy.

title: A Controlled Trial of Rivaroxaban after Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Replacement.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 1644 patients without an indication for oral anticoagulation after successful TAVR, terminated prematurely for safety.
appraisal.main_limitation: Premature termination limits precision and the mortality difference was not a prespecified primary outcome.
appraisal.one_line: GALILEO found a rivaroxaban-based strategy after TAVR increased death, thromboembolic events and bleeding versus antiplatelet therapy and was stopped early.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Death or a first thromboembolic event had occurred in 105 patients in the rivaroxaban group and in 78 patients in the antiplatelet group (incidence rates, 9.8 and 7.2 per 100 person-years, respectively; hazard ratio with rivaroxaban, 1.35; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.01 to 1.81; P = 0.04). A total of 64 deaths occurred in the rivaroxaban group and 38 in the antiplatelet group (5.8 and 3.4 per 100 person-years, respectively; hazard ratio, 1.69; 95% CI, 1.13 to 2.53).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Argues against routine anticoagulation after TAVR in patients without another indication, changing antithrombotic practice.

title: Reduced Leaflet Motion after Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Replacement.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised CT substudy, 231 patients enrolled; 97 rivaroxaban and 101 antiplatelet with evaluable scans.
appraisal.main_limitation: The primary endpoint is an imaging finding whose clinical meaning is unclear, in a substudy.
appraisal.one_line: GALILEO-4D found fewer reduced leaflet motion events with rivaroxaban than antiplatelet therapy after TAVR, despite worse clinical outcomes in the main trial.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At least one prosthetic valve leaflet with grade 3 or higher motion reduction was found in 2 of 97 patients (2.1%) who had scans that could be evaluated in the rivaroxaban group, as compared with 11 of 101 (10.9%) in the antiplatelet group (difference, -8.8 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -16.5 to -1.9; P = 0.01).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows that leaflet thrombosis can be reduced pharmacologically but that this did not translate to clinical benefit.

title: Long-term ticagrelor for secondary prevention in patients with prior myocardial infarction and no history of coronary stenting: insights from PEGASUS-TIMI 54.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified analysis of a randomised trial; 4199 of 21 162 patients had no prior coronary stenting.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis; benefit was shown with bleeding cost in the parent trial.
appraisal.one_line: PEGASUS-TIMI 54 analysis found similar relative benefit of long-term ticagrelor with and without prior stenting after MI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The relative risk reduction in MACE with ticagrelor (pooled doses) was similar in patients without (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.68-0.99) and with prior stenting (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.75-0.96; P for interaction = 0.76).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Extends the population eligible for prolonged P2Y12 inhibitor therapy beyond stented patients.

title: Polymer-based or Polymer-free Stents in Patients at High Bleeding Risk.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised noninferiority trial; 1996 patients at high bleeding risk.
appraisal.main_limitation: Noninferiority design with 1-year follow-up only.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised noninferiority comparison of two stent types in patients at high bleeding risk given one month of DAPT.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 year, the primary outcome was observed in 169 of 988 patients (17.1%) in the zotarolimus-eluting stent group and in 164 of 969 (16.9%) in the polymer-free drug-coated stent group (risk difference, 0.2 percentage points; upper boundary of the one-sided 97.5% confidence interval [CI], 3.5; noninferiority margin, 4.1; P = 0.01 for noninferiority)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs stent choice and short DAPT in a growing high-bleeding-risk population.

title: Rivaroxaban Plus Aspirin Versus Aspirin Alone in Patients With Prior Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (COMPASS-PCI).

appraisal.design_and_n: Subgroup analysis of a randomised trial; 9862 of 16 560 patients with chronic coronary syndrome had previous PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc subgroup of a trial; follow-up of 1.98 years on average.
appraisal.one_line: COMPASS substudy of dual pathway inhibition by prior PCI status in chronic coronary syndrome.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Regardless of previous PCI, DPI versus aspirin produced consistent reductions in MACE (PCI: 4.0% versus 5.5%; hazard ratio [HR], 0.74 [95% CI, 0.61-0.88]; no PCI: 4.4% versus 5.7%; HR, 0.76 [95% CI, 0.61-0.94], P-interaction=0.85)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports low-dose rivaroxaban plus aspirin in patients with prior PCI, relevant to long-term antithrombotic strategy.

title: Anticoagulation with or without Clopidogrel after Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Implantation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 157 patients on oral anticoagulation alone and 156 on oral anticoagulation plus clopidogrel.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small trial with a bleeding primary outcome; not powered for thromboembolic events.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised comparison of oral anticoagulation with or without clopidogrel after TAVI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Bleeding occurred in 34 of the 157 patients (21.7%) receiving oral anticoagulation alone and in 54 of the 156 (34.6%) receiving oral anticoagulation plus clopidogrel (risk ratio, 0.63; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.43 to 0.90; P = 0.01)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports omitting clopidogrel in TAVI patients with an indication for anticoagulation.

title: Ticagrelor With or Without Aspirin in High-Risk Patients With Diabetes Mellitus Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified subgroup analysis of a randomised trial; 2,620 patients with diabetes.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis not powered for ischaemic endpoints; high-risk selected population after 3 months of DAPT.
appraisal.one_line: Prespecified diabetes analysis of TWILIGHT: ticagrelor monotherapy reduced clinically relevant bleeding without more ischaemic events versus ticagrelor plus aspirin.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: BARC 2, 3 or 5 bleeding was 4.5% and 6.7% with ticagrelor plus placebo versus ticagrelor plus aspirin (hazard ratio: 0.65; 95% confidence interval: 0.47 to 0.91; p = 0.012); ischemic events were 4.6% vs. 5.9% (hazard ratio: 0.77; 95% confidence interval: 0.55 to 1.09; p = 0.14).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports P2Y12 monotherapy after short DAPT in patients with diabetes, a high-risk group for de-escalation strategies.

title: Ticagrelor With or Without Aspirin After Complex PCI.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified subgroup of a randomised trial; 2,342 of 7,119 patients had complex PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis; ischaemic events were few.
appraisal.one_line: TWILIGHT complex PCI subgroup of ticagrelor monotherapy versus ticagrelor plus aspirin.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared to ticagrelor plus aspirin, ticagrelor plus placebo resulted in significantly lower rates of Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) type 2, 3, or 5 bleeding (4.2% vs. 7.7%; hazard ratio [HR]: 0.54; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.38 to 0.76)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses a group at higher ischaemic risk in which aspirin withdrawal was a concern.

title: Clopidogrel versus ticagrelor or prasugrel in patients aged 70 years or older with non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome (POPular AGE): the randomised, open-label, non-inferiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 500 patients assigned to clopidogrel and 502 to ticagrelor, aged 70 years or older.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design; ticagrelor discontinuation was frequent.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised comparison of clopidogrel with ticagrelor in older patients with NSTE-ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary bleeding outcome was significantly lower in the clopidogrel group (88 [18%] of 500 patients) than in the ticagrelor group (118 [24%] of 502; hazard ratio 0·71, 95% CI 0·54 to 0·94; p=0·02 for superiority)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Challenges guideline preference for potent P2Y12 inhibitors in older patients.

title: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Oral P2Y12 Inhibitors in Acute Coronary Syndrome: Network Meta-Analysis of 52 816 Patients From 12 Randomized Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Network meta-analysis of randomised trials comparing prasugrel, ticagrelor and clopidogrel.
appraisal.main_limitation: Indirect comparisons across trials of differing populations and designs.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis of oral P2Y12 inhibitors in acute coronary syndrome.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In comparison with clopidogrel, ticagrelor significantly reduced cardiovascular mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 0.82 [95% CI, 0.72-0.92]) and all-cause mortality (HR, 0.83 [95% CI, 0.75-0.92])
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on the discordant choice between prasugrel and ticagrelor.

title: Effect of Ticagrelor Monotherapy vs Ticagrelor With Aspirin on Major Bleeding and Cardiovascular Events in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome: The TICO Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised multicentre trial; 3056 patients with ACS treated with drug-eluting stents.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design in one country; limited power for ischaemic endpoints.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of ticagrelor monotherapy after 3-month DAPT versus 12-month ticagrelor-based DAPT in ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary outcome occurred in 59 patients (3.9%) receiving ticagrelor monotherapy after 3-month DAPT and in 89 patients (5.9%) receiving ticagrelor-based 12-month DAPT (absolute difference, -1.98% [95% CI, -3.50% to -0.45%]; hazard ratio [HR], 0.66 [95% CI, 0.48 to 0.92]; P = .01)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds to evidence for short DAPT followed by P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy in ACS.

title: The Safety and Efficacy of Aspirin Discontinuation on a Background of a P2Y12 Inhibitor in Patients After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis; 32 145 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Aggregate trial-level data with differing P2Y12 inhibitors and populations.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of aspirin discontinuation on a P2Y12 inhibitor background after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Discontinuation of aspirin therapy 1 to 3 months after PCI significantly reduced the risk of major bleeding by 40% compared with dual antiplatelet therapy (1.97% versus 3.13%; hazard ratio [HR], 0.60 [95% CI, 0.45-0.79])
appraisal.why_it_matters: Consolidates the case for aspirin-free strategies after PCI.

title: Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention and Drug-Eluting Stents: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Network meta-analysis; 79 073 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Network of heterogeneous trials with indirect comparisons.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis of DAPT duration and composition after PCI with drug-eluting stents.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: extended-term DAPT was associated with a reduced risk of myocardial infarction in comparison with 12-month DAPT (absolute risk difference, -3.8 incident cases per 1000 person-years; relative risk, 0.68 [95% CI, 0.54-0.87])
appraisal.why_it_matters: Compares the full range of DAPT strategies in one framework.

title: Effect of Genotype-Guided Oral P2Y12 Inhibitor Selection vs Conventional Clopidogrel Therapy on Ischemic Outcomes After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: The TAILOR-PCI Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label randomised trial; 5302 patients undergoing PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label; primary result did not reach significance.
appraisal.one_line: Genotype-guided oral P2Y12 inhibitor selection versus clopidogrel after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred in 35 of 903 CYP2C19 LOF carriers (4.0%) in the genotype-guided therapy group and 54 of 946 (5.9%) in the conventional therapy group at 12 months (hazard ratio [HR], 0.66 [95% CI, 0.43-1.02]; P = .06)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests guided selection of P2Y12 inhibitor, a de-escalation and personalisation question.

title: Aspirin with or without Clopidogrel after Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Implantation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised controlled trial; 331 patients assigned to aspirin alone and 334 to aspirin plus clopidogrel.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label; ischaemic components were infrequent and the study was not powered for them.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised comparison of aspirin alone versus aspirin plus clopidogrel after TAVI in patients without an anticoagulation indication.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A bleeding event occurred in 50 patients (15.1%) receiving aspirin alone and in 89 (26.6%) receiving aspirin plus clopidogrel (risk ratio, 0.57; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.42 to 0.77; P = 0.001)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports single antiplatelet therapy after TAVI and is likely to inform guideline recommendations.

title: Comparison Between Ticagrelor and Clopidogrel in Elderly Patients With an Acute Coronary Syndrome: Insights From the SWEDEHEART Registry.

appraisal.design_and_n: SWEDEHEART registry cohort of 14 005 patients aged ≥80 years discharged on aspirin with clopidogrel (60.2%) or ticagrelor (39.8%), 2010 to 2017.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational with residual confounding by indication, which may explain the higher mortality.
appraisal.one_line: Registry comparison of ticagrelor and clopidogrel in patients aged 80 years or older after MI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In patients ≥80 years, the incidence of the primary ischemic outcome (hazard ratio [HR], 0.97 [95% CI, 0.88-1.06]) was similar for ticagrelor- and clopidogrel-treated patients. Ticagrelor was associated with a 17% and 48% higher risk of death (HR, 1.17 [95% CI, 1.03-1.32]) and bleeding (HR, 1.48 [95% CI, 1.25-1.76]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs P2Y12 inhibitor choice in older patients, who were under-represented in the defining trials.

title: Prasugrel-based de-escalation of dual antiplatelet therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with acute coronary syndrome (HOST-REDUCE-POLYTECH-ACS): an open-label, multicentre, non-inferiority randomised trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 2338 patients, 1170 to de-escalation and 1168 to conventional therapy.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label trial in east Asian patients; many screened patients did not meet the core indication.
appraisal.one_line: Prasugrel-based de-escalation of DAPT versus conventional DAPT after PCI in ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 82 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate 7·2%) in the de-escalation group and 116 patients (10·1%) in the conventional group (absolute risk difference -2·9%, pnon-inferiority<0·0001; hazard ratio 0·70 [95% CI 0·52-0·92], pequivalence=0·012)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports dose de-escalation of potent P2Y12 inhibitor in the post-ACS maintenance phase.

title: Timing of Oral P2Y12 Inhibitor Administration in Patients With Non-ST-Segment Elevation Acute Coronary Syndrome.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 1,449 patients, stopped early for futility.
appraisal.main_limitation: Stopped early; wide intervals.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised comparison of downstream and upstream oral P2Y12 inhibitor in NSTE-ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The rate of the primary endpoint, a composite of death due to vascular causes; nonfatal myocardial infarction or nonfatal stroke; and Bleeding Academic Research Consortium type 3, 4, and 5 bleeding through day 30, did not differ significantly between the downstream and upstream groups (percent absolute risk reduction: -0.46; 95% repeated confidence interval: -2.90 to 1.90)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on the timing of P2Y12 inhibitor loading in NSTE-ACS.

title: Validation of high bleeding risk criteria and definition as proposed by the academic research consortium for high bleeding risk.

appraisal.design_and_n: Bern PCI Registry, 16 580 participants with complete ARC-HBR criteria.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-centre registry with most criteria adjudicated retrospectively.
appraisal.one_line: External validation of the ARC high bleeding risk criteria in a large single-centre PCI registry.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: For every 0.5 score increase a step-wise augmentation of BARC 3 or 5 bleeding rates at 1 year ranging from 1.90% among patients fulfilling no criterion, through 4.01%, 5.98%, 7.42%, 8.60%, 12.21%, 12.29%, and 17.64%.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports the ARC-HBR definition that underpins antithrombotic de-escalation trials and guideline wording.

title: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Vulnerable Coronary Atherosclerotic Plaque.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 182 patients (93 BVS, 89 GDMT alone) at 15 centres after MI; NCT02171065.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small, clinical endpoints not powered, and the bioresorbable scaffold has been withdrawn.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised PROSPECT ABSORB trial: scaffold PCI of non-flow-limiting high-burden plaques enlarged lumen and was safe, with a signal for fewer lesion-related events.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Follow-up MLA was 6.9 ± 2.6 mm2 with BVS versus 3.0 ± 1.0 mm2 with GDMT alone (difference: 3.9 mm2; 95% CI 3.3 to 4.5). Target lesion failure at 24 months was 4.3% versus 4.5% (p = 0.96). Lesion-related MACE was 4.3% versus 10.7% (odds ratio 0.38; 95% CI 0.11 to 1.28).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests pre-emptive treatment of vulnerable plaque, a hypothesis-generating basis for a powered trial.

title: Ticagrelor alone vs. ticagrelor plus aspirin following percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with non-ST-segment elevation acute coronary syndromes: TWILIGHT-ACS.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified subgroup of the randomised TWILIGHT trial (NCT02270242); NSTE-ACS n=4614, stable n=2503, of 7119 randomised.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis, not powered for ischaemic outcomes; high-risk, adherent, event-free patients only.
appraisal.one_line: TWILIGHT-ACS: ticagrelor monotherapy after 3 months of DAPT reduced bleeding in NSTE-ACS without more ischaemic events.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In NSTE-ACS, BARC 2, 3 or 5 bleeding was 3.6% vs 7.6% (HR 0.47; 95% CI 0.36-0.61; P < 0.001); in stable patients 4.8% vs 6.2% (HR 0.76; 95% CI 0.54-1.06; P = 0.11). Death, MI or stroke was 4.3% vs 4.4% (HR 0.97; 95% CI 0.74-1.28) with NSTE-ACS.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports P2Y12 monotherapy after short DAPT as a de-escalation option in NSTE-ACS.

title: Long-term efficacy and safety of drug-coated balloons versus drug-eluting stents for small coronary artery disease (BASKET-SMALL 2): 3-year follow-up of a randomised, non-inferiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised, open-label, non-inferiority trial; 758 patients (DCB n=382, DES n=376); NCT01574534.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, not powered for individual components and mostly stable disease.
appraisal.one_line: BASKET-SMALL 2 at 3 years: drug-coated balloons remained comparable to drug-eluting stents in small coronary vessels.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Kaplan-Meier MACE was 15% in both groups (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.68-1.45; p=0.95). Cardiac death HR 1.29 (0.63-2.66); all-cause death HR 1.05 (0.62-1.77); major bleeding HR 0.43 (0.17-1.13).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Longer-term evidence for DCB-only strategies in small vessels.

title: Association of Ticagrelor vs Clopidogrel With Net Adverse Clinical Events in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective cohort in two US EHR databases and one South Korean database; 31 290 propensity-matched pairs.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational with possible unmeasured confounding; the authors state this.
appraisal.one_line: Multi-database observational comparison found no significant NACE difference between ticagrelor and clopidogrel after PCI for ACS but more bleeding and dyspnoea with ticagrelor.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The 1-year risk of NACE was 15.1% vs 14.6% (summary HR, 1.05 [95% CI, 1.00-1.10]; P = .06). Hemorrhagic events were 2.1% vs 1.6% (summary HR, 1.35 [95% CI, 1.13-1.61]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Real-world check on the guideline preference for ticagrelor over clopidogrel.

title: Ticagrelor or Prasugrel in Patients With ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction Undergoing Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified subgroup of the randomised ISAR-REACT 5 trial (NCT01944800); 1653 patients with STEMI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis in an open-label trial; MI finding not adjusted for multiplicity.
appraisal.one_line: ISAR-REACT 5 STEMI subgroup: no significant difference in death, MI or stroke between ticagrelor and prasugrel, with more MI on ticagrelor.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary end point occurred in 83 patients (10.1%) with ticagrelor and 64 (7.9%) with prasugrel (hazard ratio, 1.31 [95% CI, 0.95-1.82]; P=0.10). Myocardial infarction was 5.3% vs 2.8% (hazard ratio, 1.95 [95% CI, 1.18-3.23]; P=0.010).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs choice of potent P2Y12 inhibitor in primary PCI.

title: Reduction in Revascularization With Icosapent Ethyl: Insights From REDUCE-IT Revascularization Analyses.

appraisal.design_and_n: Post hoc analysis of the randomised REDUCE-IT trial (NCT01492361); 8179 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Exploratory analysis of a trial whose mineral-oil comparator is debated; population is not an interventional cohort.
appraisal.one_line: REDUCE-IT revascularisation analysis: icosapent ethyl reduced first and total coronary revascularisations.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: First revascularizations were 9.2% with icosapent ethyl vs 13.3% with placebo (hazard ratio, 0.66 [95% CI, 0.58-0.76]; P<0.0001); PCI hazard ratio 0.68 [95% CI, 0.59-0.79]; CABG hazard ratio 0.61 [95% CI, 0.45-0.81].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Describes a lipid-lowering effect on revascularisation burden.

title: Ticagrelor versus clopidogrel in elective percutaneous coronary intervention (ALPHEUS): a randomised, open-label, phase 3b trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised, open-label, phase 3b trial; 1910 randomised (ticagrelor 956, clopidogrel 954) at 49 sites.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, biomarker-defined primary outcome rather than clinical events.
appraisal.one_line: ALPHEUS: ticagrelor was not superior to clopidogrel for periprocedural myonecrosis after high-risk elective PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 48 h, the primary outcome occurred in 334 (35%) of 941 patients on ticagrelor and 341 (36%) of 942 on clopidogrel (odds ratio 0.97, 95% CI 0.80-1.17; p=0.75). Minor bleeding at 30 days was 105 (11%) vs 71 (8%) (OR 1.54, 95% CI 1.12-2.11).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports clopidogrel as standard in elective PCI and informs the periprocedural MI debate.

title: Durable Polymer Versus Biodegradable Polymer Drug-Eluting Stents After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Patients with Acute Coronary Syndrome: The HOST-REDUCE-POLYTECH-ACS Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised, open-label, adjudicator-blinded, non-inferiority trial; 3413 patients (DP-DES 1713, BP-DES 1700); NCT02193971.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label; 12-month follow-up and driven by target lesion revascularisation.
appraisal.one_line: HOST-REDUCE-POLYTECH-ACS: durable-polymer DES was non-inferior to biodegradable-polymer DES for patient-oriented outcomes in ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Patient-oriented composite at 12 months was 5.2% with DP-DES and 6.4% with BP-DES (absolute risk difference, -1.2%; Pnoninferiority<0.001). Device-oriented composite was 2.6% vs 3.9% (hazard ratio, 0.67 [95% CI, 0.46-0.98]; P=0.038).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large randomised comparison of stent polymer technology in ACS.

title: Ticagrelor or Prasugrel in Patients With Non-ST-Segment Elevation Acute Coronary Syndromes.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Post hoc pooled analysis of the unstable angina and NSTEMI subgroups of the randomised ISAR-REACT 5 trial (NCT01944800); ticagrelor 1,179, prasugrel 1,186.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc nature; open-label design; authors state confirmation is needed.
appraisal.one_line: Post hoc ISAR-REACT 5 analysis in NSTE-ACS: prasugrel was associated with fewer death, MI or stroke events than ticagrelor.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 101 (8.7%) with ticagrelor and 73 (6.3%) with prasugrel (hazard ratio 1.41; 95% CI 1.04 to 1.90). Safety endpoint HR 1.09; 95% CI 0.72 to 1.65.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on the choice of potent P2Y12 inhibitor in NSTE-ACS where guidelines diverge.

title: Short dual antiplatelet therapy followed by P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy vs. prolonged dual antiplatelet therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention with second-generation drug-eluting stents: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 5 randomised trials, 32 145 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Few trials, heterogeneous populations and SAPT strategies; stent thrombosis imprecisely estimated.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of five trials: 1 to 3 months of DAPT then P2Y12 inhibitor SAPT lowered major bleeding versus 12 months of DAPT after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Major bleeding was lower with short DAPT followed by P2Y12 inhibitor SAPT (random-effects model: HR 0.63, 95% 0.45-0.86); stent thrombosis HR 1.19 (95% CI 0.86-1.65); all-cause death HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.70-1.03).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Pools trials behind guideline de-escalation recommendations.

title: Effect of Prehospital Crushed Prasugrel Tablets in Patients With ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction Planned for Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: The Randomized COMPARE CRUSH Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised multicentre trial, 727 patients; NCT03296540.
appraisal.main_limitation: Surrogate primary outcome; short time to PCI.
appraisal.one_line: Prehospital crushed prasugrel did not improve TIMI 3 flow or ST resolution in STEMI despite lower platelet reactivity.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: TIMI 3 flow before pPCI occurred in 31.0% crushed vs 32.7% integral (odds ratio, 0.92 [95% CI, 0.65-1.30], P=0.64); complete ST resolution 59.9% vs 57.3% (odds ratio, 1.11 [95% CI, 0.78-1.58]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Negative trial on a common prehospital practice in STEMI.

title: 2020 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Valvular Heart Disease: Executive Summary: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Joint Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines.

appraisal.design_and_n: Guideline executive summary; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Many recommendations rest on lower levels of evidence; the abstract gives no class or level detail.
appraisal.one_line: 2020 ACC/AHA valvular heart disease guideline executive summary, including timing and choice of surgical and catheter interventions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Primary US reference for TAVI, mitral and tricuspid intervention decisions, to compare with ESC guidance.

title: 2020 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Valvular Heart Disease: Executive Summary: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Joint Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Guideline executive summary; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Same document as the Circulation publication; recommendation levels not given in the abstract.
appraisal.one_line: 2020 ACC/AHA valvular heart disease guideline executive summary (JACC publication), covering diagnostic work-up and timing and choice of interventions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Primary US reference for valve intervention decisions; duplicate publication of the same guideline.

title: 10-Year Follow-Up of Patients With Everolimus-Eluting Versus Bare-Metal Stents After ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial follow-up; 1,498 patients (EES 751, BMS 747); NCT04462315.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label extension; composite driven mainly by target lesion revascularisation.
appraisal.one_line: EXAMINATION-EXTEND: at 10 years, everolimus-eluting stents had fewer patient- and device-oriented events than bare-metal stents after STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Patient-oriented composite was 32.4% vs 38.0% (HR 0.81; 95% CI 0.68 to 0.96; p = 0.013) and device-oriented composite 13.6% vs 18.4% (HR 0.72; 95% CI 0.55 to 0.93; p = 0.012).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Longest follow-up of DES versus BMS in primary PCI.

title: Primary Outcome Evaluation of a Next-Generation Left Atrial Appendage Closure Device: Results From the PINNACLE FLX Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: PINNACLE FLX (NCT02702271), prospective nonrandomised multicentre study, 400 patients enrolled.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-arm design with an anatomic closure endpoint rather than clinical efficacy.
appraisal.one_line: Single-arm FDA study of the Watchman FLX left atrial appendage closure device met both performance goals.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The incidence of the primary safety end point was 0.5% with a 1-sided 95% upper CI of 1.6%, meeting the performance goal of 4.2% (P<0.0001). The incidence of the primary effectiveness end point was 100%, with a 1-sided 95% lower CI of 99.1%, again meeting the performance goal of 97.0% (P<0.0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Regulatory evidence for the next-generation LAAO device in an adjacent intervention domain.

title: Management of antithrombotic therapy in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a consensus document of the ESC Working Group on Thrombosis and the European Association of Percutaneous Cardiovascular Interventions (EAPCI), in collaboration with the ESC Council on Valvular Heart Disease.

appraisal.design_and_n: Consensus document; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Consensus document; prior recommendations were mostly based on expert opinion.
appraisal.one_line: ESC Working Group consensus document updating antithrombotic management during and after TAVI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Updates European guidance on antithrombotic therapy after TAVI in light of recent randomised trials.

title: Guided versus standard antiplatelet therapy in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 randomised trials and 3 observational studies; 20 743 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Mixed randomised and observational data, heterogeneous guidance strategies and endpoint definitions.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis: guided antiplatelet therapy reduced MACE after PCI versus standard therapy, with escalation lowering ischaemic events and de-escalation lowering bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Guided selection reduced major adverse cardiovascular events (RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.63-0.95, p=0.015) and bleeding, not significantly (RR 0.88, 0.77-1.01, p=0.069). All-cause death and major bleeding did not differ.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on guided de-escalation and escalation of P2Y12 therapy in PCI.

title: Diabetes-Related Factors and the Effects of Ticagrelor Plus Aspirin in the THEMIS and THEMIS-PCI Trials.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Post hoc analyses of the randomised THEMIS (n = 19,220) and THEMIS-PCI trials.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc subgroup analyses without multiplicity control.
appraisal.one_line: THEMIS and THEMIS-PCI: relative effects of ticagrelor plus aspirin were consistent across diabetes duration, HbA1c and antihyperglycaemic therapy.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 3-point MACE reduction with ticagrelor plus aspirin (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.90; p = 0.04) was generally consistent across subgroups; major bleeding was increased (HR: 2.32; p < 0.001) similarly across subgroups.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs long-term ticagrelor plus aspirin in diabetes with coronary disease.

title: Aspirin versus clopidogrel for chronic maintenance monotherapy after percutaneous coronary intervention (HOST-EXAM): an investigator-initiated, prospective, randomised, open-label, multicentre trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Investigator-initiated, open-label randomised trial in South Korea; 5438 randomised (clopidogrel 2710, aspirin 2728).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, single-country population, composite endpoint including readmission.
appraisal.one_line: HOST-EXAM: clopidogrel monotherapy reduced a composite of death, MI, stroke, ACS readmission and major bleeding versus aspirin monotherapy in chronic maintenance after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary outcome occurred in 152 (5.7%) patients in the clopidogrel group and 207 (7.7%) in the aspirin group (hazard ratio 0.73 [95% CI 0.59-0.90]; p=0.0035).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Directly addresses which single antiplatelet to use long term after PCI.

title: P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy or dual antiplatelet therapy after coronary revascularisation: individual patient level meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient level meta-analysis of 6 randomised trials, 24 096 patients; PROSPERO CRD42020176853.
appraisal.main_limitation: Sex interaction is exploratory; trial designs and loading strategies differed.
appraisal.one_line: IPD meta-analysis of six trials: P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy was non-inferior to DAPT for death, MI or stroke and lowered bleeding after revascularisation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary outcome occurred in 283 (2.95%) with monotherapy and 315 (3.27%) with DAPT in the per protocol population (hazard ratio 0.93, 95% confidence interval 0.79 to 1.09; P=0.005 for non-inferiority). BARC 3 or 5 bleeding: hazard ratio 0.49, 0.39 to 0.63; P<0.001.
appraisal.why_it_matters: IPD evidence on de-escalation of antiplatelet therapy, with a sex-specific signal.

title: De-Escalation of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Network meta-analysis of 15 RCTs, 55,798 patients with ACS.
appraisal.main_limitation: Bleeding was trial-defined major or minor, so definitions vary across trials; the abstract does not describe heterogeneity or consistency checks.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis of 15 randomised trials in acute coronary syndromes found that DAPT de-escalation reduced bleeding without a detectable rise in ischaemic events.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: De-escalation was associated with reduced primary bleeding (HR: 0.48 [95% CI: 0.30-0.77] vs clopidogrel; HR: 0.32 [95% CI: 0.20-0.52] vs ticagrelor; HR: 0.36 [95% CI: 0.24-0.55] vs standard-dose prasugrel; HR: 0.40 [95% CI: 0.22-0.75] vs low-dose prasugrel) without negatively affecting primary efficacy outcomes.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Pools the de-escalation trials on a common basis, relevant to the antiplatelet strategy after ACS and to updating guideline recommendations.

title: Predictors of Device-Related Thrombus Following Percutaneous Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: International multicentre case-control style registry, 711 patients (237 with and 474 without DRT) from 37 centres.
appraisal.main_limitation: Matched sampling of non-DRT cases and wide confidence intervals for several predictors.
appraisal.one_line: Multicentre registry identified predictors of device-related thrombus after LAAO and linked it to ischaemic events.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: DRT presence was associated with a higher risk of the composite endpoint of death, ischemic stroke, or systemic embolization (HR: 2.37; 95% CI, 1.58-3.56; P < 0.001) driven by ischemic stroke (HR: 3.49; 95% CI: 1.35-9.00; P = 0.01).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports risk stratification and antithrombotic decisions after LAAO.

title: Antiplatelet therapy in patients with conservatively managed spontaneous coronary artery dissection from the multicentre DISCO registry.

appraisal.design_and_n: DISCO multicentre registry, 199 conservatively managed patients (NCT04415762).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small non-randomised sample with confounding by indication.
appraisal.one_line: In conservatively managed SCAD, DAPT was associated with more MACE at 1 year than single antiplatelet therapy.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Patients treated with DAPT had a significantly higher MACE rate than those with SAPT [18.9% vs. 6.0% hazard ratios (HR) 2.62; 95% confidence intervals (CI) 1.22-5.61; P = 0.013].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Antiplatelet strategy in SCAD is unsettled and the signal challenges routine DAPT.

title: Edoxaban versus Vitamin K Antagonist for Atrial Fibrillation after TAVR.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised open-label, adjudicator-masked trial, 1426 patients (713 per group), mean age 82.1 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design, and noninferiority for major bleeding was not shown.
appraisal.one_line: ENVISAGE-TAVI AF found edoxaban noninferior to vitamin K antagonists for a composite of adverse events after TAVR, with more major bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The composite primary efficacy outcome was 17.3 per 100 person-years with edoxaban and 16.5 with vitamin K antagonists (hazard ratio, 1.05; 95% CI, 0.85 to 1.31; P = 0.01 for noninferiority). Major bleeding was 9.7 vs. 7.0 per 100 person-years (hazard ratio, 1.40; 95% CI, 1.03 to 1.91; P = 0.93 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Directly informs oral anticoagulant choice in patients with atrial fibrillation after TAVR, with a safety signal for gastrointestinal bleeding.

title: Dual Antiplatelet Therapy after PCI in Patients at High Bleeding Risk.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 4434 patients in the per-protocol population and 4579 in the intention-to-treat population.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design, noninferiority margins for ischaemic outcomes, and results apply to one stent platform.
appraisal.one_line: MASTER DAPT showed that one month of DAPT after a biodegradable-polymer sirolimus-eluting stent was noninferior to a longer course in high bleeding risk patients, with less bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Net adverse clinical events occurred in 165 patients (7.5%) with abbreviated therapy and 172 (7.7%) with standard therapy (difference, -0.23 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.80 to 1.33; P<0.001 for noninferiority). Major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding was 148 (6.5%) vs. 211 (9.4%) (difference, -2.82 percentage points; 95% CI, -4.40 to -1.24; P<0.001 for superiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large trial in a common high-risk group that supports shortening DAPT to one month after PCI and bears directly on guideline recommendations for high bleeding risk.

title: Unguided de-escalation from ticagrelor to clopidogrel in stabilised patients with acute myocardial infarction undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (TALOS-AMI): an investigator-initiated, open-label, multicentre, non-inferiority, randomised trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised open-label noninferiority trial, 2697 patients (1349 de-escalation, 1348 control) in South Korea.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, single-country, and underpowered for ischaemic events alone.
appraisal.one_line: TALOS-AMI found that unguided de-escalation from ticagrelor to clopidogrel after the first month reduced net clinical events after myocardial infarction, mainly through less bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 59 (4·6%) vs 104 (8·2%) patients (pnon-inferiority<0·001; HR 0·55 [95% CI 0·40-0·76], psuperiority=0·0001). Cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or stroke was 2·1% vs 3·1% (HR 0·69; 95% CI 0·42-1·14, p=0·15).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds randomised evidence for uniform de-escalation in an Asian population, bearing on antiplatelet strategy after myocardial infarction.

title: Amulet or Watchman Device for Percutaneous Left Atrial Appendage Closure: Primary Results of the SWISS-APERO Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised open-label trial, 221 patients at 8 European centres.
appraisal.main_limitation: Imaging surrogate primary endpoint and short follow-up of 45 days.
appraisal.one_line: SWISS-APERO found no difference in a composite of crossover or residual appendage patency between Amulet and Watchman at 45 days, with more procedural complications with Amulet.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred in 71 (67.6%) patients receiving Amulet and 70 (70.0%) receiving Watchman (risk ratio, 0.97 [95% CI, 0.80-1.16]; P=0.713). Major procedure-related complications were 9.0% vs. 2.7% (P=0.047).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Head-to-head device data in an adjacent intervention, with a safety signal for Amulet.

title: Duration of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy for Patients at High Bleeding Risk Undergoing PCI.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: XIENCE Short DAPT programme of three single-arm studies, 3,652 enrolled; 1,392 on 1-month and 1,972 on 3-month DAPT.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised exploratory comparison across single-arm studies.
appraisal.one_line: Exploratory pooled analysis of HBR patients found 1-month DAPT had similar ischaemic outcomes and less bleeding than 3-month DAPT.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint of all-cause mortality or myocardial infarction was similar between the 2 groups (7.3% vs 7.5%; difference -0.2%; 95% CI: -2.2% to 1.7%; P = 0.41). BARC type 2-5 bleeding was lower with 1-month DAPT (7.6% vs 10.0%; difference -2.5%; 95% CI: -4.6% to -0.3%; P = 0.012).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses optimal DAPT duration in high bleeding risk patients.

title: 2021 ACC/AHA/SCAI Guideline for Coronary Artery Revascularization: Executive Summary: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Joint Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Clinical practice guideline (executive summary).
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract does not list recommendation classes or levels; this is a parallel publication of an item already stored.
appraisal.one_line: Executive summary of the 2021 ACC/AHA/SCAI coronary artery revascularisation guideline (duplicate publication in a second journal).
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Parallel publication of the American revascularisation guideline summary.

title: Comparative effects of guided vs. potent P2Y12 inhibitor therapy in acute coronary syndrome: a network meta-analysis of 61 898 patients from 15 randomized trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Network meta-analysis of 15 RCTs, 61 898 patients; PROSPERO CRD42021258603.
appraisal.main_limitation: Indirect comparisons across heterogeneous trials of guided strategies and fixed agents.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis found that guided selection of P2Y12 inhibitor therapy was the only strategy associated with fewer MACE without more bleeding in ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A guided approach was associated with reduced MACE (IRR: 0.80, 95% CI: 0.65-0.98) without any significant trade-off in all bleeding (IRR: 1.22, 95% CI: 0.96-1.55).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on guided versus potent P2Y12 inhibitor therapy, with relevance to guideline recommendations.

title: Antithrombotic Therapy in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation After Acute Coronary Syndromes or Percutaneous Intervention.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified-style subgroup analysis of a 2 x 2 factorial randomised trial; 4,386 of 4,614 patients with calculable scores.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis, and the trial was not powered for ischaemic outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: AUGUSTUS secondary analysis found that apixaban without aspirin reduced bleeding irrespective of baseline bleeding or stroke risk scores in atrial fibrillation with ACS or PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Bleeding rates were lower with apixaban than VKA (HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.41-0.78 [HAS-BLED ≤2]; HR: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.59-0.88 [HAS-BLED ≥3]; interaction P = 0.23). Aspirin increased bleeding (HR: 1.86; 95% CI: 1.36-2.56 [HAS-BLED ≤2]; HR: 1.81; 95% CI: 1.47-2.23 [HAS-BLED ≥3]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports omitting aspirin and using apixaban across risk strata in patients on oral anticoagulation after ACS or PCI.

title: Edoxaban Versus Dual Antiplatelet Therapy for Leaflet Thrombosis and Cerebral Thromboembolism After TAVR: The ADAPT-TAVR Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised open-label trial, 229 patients in the intention-to-treat population.
appraisal.main_limitation: Underpowered, as the authors state, with imaging endpoints.
appraisal.one_line: ADAPT-TAVR found numerically lower leaflet thrombosis with edoxaban than DAPT after TAVR, but the difference was not significant.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Leaflet thrombosis was 9.8% vs 18.4% (absolute difference, -8.5% [95% CI, -17.8% to 0.8%]; P=0.076). New cerebral lesions were 25.0% vs 20.2% (difference, 4.8%; 95% CI, -6.4% to 16.0%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs antithrombotic therapy after TAVR in patients without an anticoagulation indication.

title: Antithrombotic Therapy After Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: NCDR LAAO Registry analysis of 31,994 patients undergoing successful Watchman LAAO between 2016 and 2018.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational comparison with residual confounding by indication.
appraisal.one_line: Antithrombotic regimens after LAAO in US practice and their association with adverse events.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Only 12.2% received the full postprocedure treatment protocol studied in pivotal trials. The adjusted risk of any adverse event through 45 days was lower for discharge on warfarin alone (HR: 0.692; 95% CI: 0.569-0.841) and DOAC alone (HR: 0.731; 95% CI: 0.574-0.930) compared with warfarin and aspirin.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It shows wide deviation from trial protocols and a signal favouring regimens without aspirin, a question suited to randomised testing.

title: Apixaban vs. standard of care after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: the ATLANTIS trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: International randomised open-label superiority trial; 1500 patients (749 apixaban, 751 standard of care).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design with a broad composite; stratum analyses were exploratory, and a higher non-cardiovascular mortality signal was observed with apixaban.
appraisal.one_line: ATLANTIS randomised 1500 patients after TAVI to apixaban or standard of care; apixaban was not superior on the composite primary endpoint.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary outcome occurred in 138 (18.4%) and 151 (20.1%) patients receiving apixaban or standard of care, respectively [hazard ratio (HR) 0.92; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.73-1.16]; the primary safety endpoint was similar (HR 1.02; 95% CI 0.72-1.44).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large randomised evidence on antithrombotic therapy after TAVI that bears directly on guideline recommendations for anticoagulation versus antiplatelet therapy.

title: Association of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy With Ticagrelor With Vein Graft Failure After Coronary Artery Bypass Graft Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: IPD meta-analysis of randomised trials; 4 RCTs with 1316 patients and 1668 saphenous vein grafts.
appraisal.main_limitation: Graft patency is an imaging endpoint rather than a clinical event, and the trials were small and few.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data meta-analysis found ticagrelor DAPT was associated with less saphenous vein graft failure than aspirin after CABG, at the cost of more BARC 2, 3 or 5 bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Ticagrelor DAPT was associated with a significantly lower incidence of saphenous vein graft failure (11.2%) per graft than was aspirin (20%; difference, -8.7% [95% CI, -13.5% to -3.9%]; OR, 0.51 [95% CI, 0.35 to 0.74]; P < .001); BARC type 2, 3, or 5 bleeding was higher (OR, 2.98 [95% CI, 1.99 to 4.47]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs antithrombotic choice after CABG, a decision at the PCI versus CABG interface, though clinical-event benefit is not shown.

title: Impact of Medication Nonadherence in a Clinical Trial of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
