appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of a randomised trial; 4,579 high bleeding risk patients, using inverse probability-of-censoring weights.
appraisal.main_limitation: Adherence-corrected analysis is non-randomised in nature, and the reported confidence interval for MCB does not enclose its point estimate.
appraisal.one_line: MASTER DAPT adherence analysis in high bleeding risk patients found that abbreviated DAPT was associated with similar NACE and MACE and lower bleeding after correcting for nonadherence.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: NACE (HR: 1.01; 95% CI: 0.88-1.27) or MACE (HR: 1.07; 95% CI: 0.83-1.40) did not differ, and MCB was lower with abbreviated compared with standard treatment (HR: 0.51; 95% CI: 0.60-0.73).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports the robustness of the abbreviated DAPT result in high bleeding risk patients (D8).

title: A Multicenter, Phase 2, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Double-Blind, Parallel-Group, Dose-Finding Trial of the Oral Factor XIa Inhibitor Asundexian to Prevent Adverse Cardiovascular Outcomes After Acute Myocardial Infarction.

appraisal.design_and_n: Phase 2 randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; 1601 patients with recent acute MI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Dose-finding trial with few ischaemic events and 90% confidence intervals, not powered for efficacy.
appraisal.one_line: Phase 2 dose-ranging trial of the factor XIa inhibitor asundexian after acute MI showed near-complete FXIa inhibition without a significant increase in bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The main safety outcome occurred in 30 (7.6%), 32 (8.1%), 42 (10.5%), and 36 (9.0%) patients receiving asundexian 10 mg, 20 mg, or 50 mg, or placebo, respectively (pooled asundexian versus placebo: hazard ratio, 0.98 [90% CI, 0.71-1.35]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: First factor XI inhibitor data on top of DAPT after MI, relevant to future antithrombotic strategies (D8).

title: Management of Patients at Risk for and With Left Ventricular Thrombus: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.

appraisal.design_and_n: Scientific statement from the American Heart Association; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Consensus suggestions where randomised data are limited.
appraisal.one_line: AHA scientific statement addresses eight management questions on LV thrombus, including DOACs versus warfarin and anticoagulation after MI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Covers LV thrombus management (D8), where guideline recommendations are sparse.

title: Abbreviated Antiplatelet Therapy After Coronary Stenting in Patients With Myocardial Infarction at High Bleeding Risk.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified subgroup analysis of a randomised trial; 4,579 patients at HBR, of whom 1,780 had acute or recent MI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis, with limited power for ischaemic events within the MI stratum.
appraisal.one_line: MASTER DAPT analysis by presence of recent MI found that 1-month DAPT in high bleeding risk patients gave similar NACE and MACCE and less bleeding irrespective of MI presentation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: NACE and MACCE did not differ with abbreviated vs nonabbreviated APT regimens in patients with an acute or recent myocardial infarction (n = 1,780; HR: 0.83; 95% CI: 0.61-1.12 and HR: 0.86; 95% CI: 0.62-1.19, respectively).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Extends abbreviated DAPT evidence to high bleeding risk patients with MI (D8, D6).

title: Indobufen or Aspirin on Top of Clopidogrel After Coronary Drug-Eluting Stent Implantation (OPTION): A Randomized, Open-Label, End Point-Blinded, Noninferiority Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised, open-label, endpoint-blinded noninferiority trial in 103 Chinese centres; 4551 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, troponin-negative patients only, clopidogrel as P2Y12 inhibitor, and a Chinese population limiting generalisability.
appraisal.one_line: OPTION randomised patients after drug-eluting stents to indobufen or aspirin plus clopidogrel and found a lower net clinical composite driven by less bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred in 101 patients (4.47%) in the indobufen-based DAPT group and 140 patients (6.11%) in the conventional DAPT group (absolute difference, -1.63%; Pnoninferiority<0.001; hazard ratio, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.56-0.94]; P=0.015).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests an aspirin alternative within DAPT after PCI (D8) in a large randomised sample.

title: Aspirin Versus Clopidogrel for Long-Term Maintenance Monotherapy After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: The HOST-EXAM Extended Study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Post-trial follow-up of a randomised trial; 5438 patients randomised, per-protocol analysis of 2431 clopidogrel and 2286 aspirin patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post-trial extension analysed per protocol, open to attrition and treatment crossover bias, in an East Asian population.
appraisal.one_line: HOST-EXAM extended follow-up found clopidogrel monotherapy was associated with a lower net clinical composite than aspirin monotherapy over more than 5 years after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: During a median follow-up of 5.8 years (interquartile range, 4.8-6.2 years), the primary end point occurred in 12.8% and 16.9% in the clopidogrel and aspirin groups, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.74 [95% CI, 0.63-0.86]; P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the choice of long-term single antiplatelet agent after PCI (D8).

title: Bivalirudin plus a high-dose infusion versus heparin monotherapy in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention: a randomised trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Investigator-initiated, open-label randomised trial at 87 Chinese centres; 6016 patients (3009 bivalirudin, 3007 heparin).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, Chinese centres with predominantly radial access, and an industry research grant; 30-day follow-up only.
appraisal.one_line: BRIGHT-4 randomised STEMI patients to bivalirudin with a post-PCI high-dose infusion or heparin monotherapy; bivalirudin reduced 30-day death or major bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with heparin monotherapy, bivalirudin reduced the 30-day rate of the primary endpoint (132 events [4·39%] in the heparin group vs 92 events [3·06%] in the bivalirudin group; difference, 1·33%, 95% CI 0·38-2·29%; hazard ratio [HR] 0·69, 95% CI 0·53-0·91; p=0·0070).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large randomised evidence on anticoagulation in primary PCI (D8, D6) that bears on guideline recommendations for bivalirudin versus heparin.

title: Dual antiplatelet therapy duration after percutaneous coronary intervention in high bleeding risk: a meta-analysis of randomized trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials; 11 trials including 9006 HBR patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial-level pooling across varying HBR definitions and DAPT strategies; patients with an indication for oral anticoagulation were excluded.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of randomised trials in high bleeding risk patients found 1-month or 3-month DAPT reduced bleeding and cardiovascular mortality without more ischaemic events.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Abbreviated DAPT reduced major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding [risk ratio (RR): 0.76, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.61-0.94; I2 = 28%], major bleeding (RR: 0.80, 95% CI: 0.64-0.99, I2 = 0%), and cardiovascular mortality (RR: 0.79, 95% CI: 0.65-0.95, I2 = 0%) compared with standard DAPT.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Summarises the evidence for DAPT de-escalation in high bleeding risk PCI (D8).

title: P2Y12 Inhibitor Monotherapy or Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Complex Percutaneous Coronary Interventions.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled patient-level data from 5 randomised trials including 22,941 patients, of whom 4,685 (20.4%) had complex PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis by PCI complexity, with few events in the complex group and a short-DAPT lead-in that differs between trials.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data meta-analysis of P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy versus DAPT by complexity of PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary efficacy endpoint was similar between strategies in complex PCI (HR: 0.87; 95% CI: 0.64-1.19) and noncomplex PCI (HR: 0.91; 95% CI: 0.76-1.09); BARC 3 or 5 bleeding was lower with monotherapy in complex PCI (HR: 0.51; 95% CI: 0.31-0.84).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses whether shortened DAPT is safe in higher-risk anatomy, a common decision in antithrombotic de-escalation.

title: Comparative Effectiveness of Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion Versus Oral Anticoagulation by Sex.

appraisal.design_and_n: Medicare claims cohort; 4085 women and 5378 men with LAAO were matched 1:1 to anticoagulation recipients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Propensity-matched claims data with residual confounding; the large mortality difference suggests selection effects.
appraisal.one_line: Medicare comparison of LAAO with anticoagulation, by sex.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: LAAO was associated with lower mortality in women and men (hazard ratio [HR], 0.509 [95% CI, 0.447-0.580]; and HR, 0.541 [95% CI, 0.487-0.601], respectively) and lower stroke or systemic embolism (HR, 0.655 [95% CI, 0.555-0.772]; and HR, 0.649 [95% CI, 0.552-0.762]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It adds sex-specific real-world data to the LAAO versus anticoagulation debate, though randomised evidence remains decisive.

title: Comparison of 3- to 6-Month Versus 12-Month Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Coronary Intervention Using the Contemporary Drug-Eluting Stents With Ultrathin Struts: The HOST-IDEA Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label randomised trial at 37 centres in South Korea; 2013 patients randomised to 3- to 6-month DAPT (n=1002) or 12-month DAPT (n=1011).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design in a single country with physician choice of antiplatelet agent and exclusion of STEMI.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised noninferiority trial of 3- to 6-month versus 12-month DAPT after ultrathin-strut DES.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary outcome occurred in 37 (3.7%) patients versus 41 (4.1%); noninferiority was met (absolute risk difference, -0.4% [1-sided 95% CI, -∞% to 1.1%]; P<0.001 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds to evidence supporting shortened DAPT after contemporary stents.

title: Dual antiplatelet therapy de-escalation in acute coronary syndrome: an individual patient meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient data meta-analysis of four RCTs including 10 133 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Pooled trials differ in the de-escalation approach (guided versus unguided, and drug switching), and open-label designs may bias bleeding reports.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data meta-analysis of DAPT de-escalation versus standard DAPT after PCI for acute coronary syndrome.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The ischaemic endpoint was lower with de-escalation than standard strategy (2.3% vs. 3.0%, hazard ratio [HR] 0.761, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.597-0.972), and bleeding was lower (6.5% vs. 9.1%, HR 0.701, 95% CI 0.606-0.811).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports de-escalation of antiplatelet therapy after ACS, a common decision.

title: Defining Strategies of Modulation of Antiplatelet Therapy in Patients With Coronary Artery Disease: A Consensus Document from the Academic Research Consortium.

appraisal.design_and_n: Consensus document from the Academic Research Consortium.
appraisal.main_limitation: Terminology and definitions rather than new outcome evidence.
appraisal.one_line: Academic Research Consortium consensus defining strategies of antiplatelet therapy modulation in coronary artery disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Standardises de-escalation and escalation terminology used across antithrombotic trials and guidelines.

title: P2Y12 Inhibitor or Aspirin Monotherapy for Secondary Prevention of Coronary Events.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient data meta-analysis of 7 trials; 24,325 participants, 12,178 assigned to P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy and 12,147 to aspirin.
appraisal.main_limitation: Mostly clopidogrel and ticagrelor trials with differing populations and open-label designs.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data meta-analysis of P2Y12 inhibitor versus aspirin monotherapy for long-term secondary prevention in coronary disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Risk of the primary outcome was lower with P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy compared with aspirin over 2 years (HR: 0.88; 95% CI: 0.79-0.97; P = 0.012), with similar major bleeding (HR: 0.87; 95% CI: 0.70-1.09; P = 0.23).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Challenges aspirin as default chronic antiplatelet agent and bears on guideline recommendations.

title: STREAM-2: Half-Dose Tenecteplase or Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Older Patients With ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Randomized, Open-Label Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label randomised trial; patients assigned to pharmaco-invasive treatment (n=401) or primary PCI (n=203).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, with a 2:1 allocation and small numbers for clinical events; six intracranial haemorrhages occurred in the pharmaco-invasive arm.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of half-dose tenecteplase pharmaco-invasive treatment versus primary PCI in older patients with STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The composite clinical end point occurred in 12.8% (51/400) of patients undergoing pharmaco-invasive treatment and 13.3% (27/203) of patients undergoing primary PCI (relative risk, 0.96 [95% CI, 0.62-1.48]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs reperfusion choice in older patients when primary PCI is delayed.

title: 2023 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Chronic Coronary Disease: A Report of the American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology Joint Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines.

appraisal.design_and_n: Clinical practice guideline based on a literature search from September 2021 to May 2022.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract gives no recommendation classes or levels.
appraisal.one_line: 2023 AHA/ACC multisociety guideline for the management of chronic coronary disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Replaces the 2012 and 2014 stable ischaemic heart disease guidance and sets US positions on revascularisation and antithrombotic therapy.

title: 2023 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Chronic Coronary Disease: A Report of the American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology Joint Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Clinical practice guideline based on a literature search from September 2021 to May 2022; companion publication of the same guideline.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract gives no recommendation classes or levels.
appraisal.one_line: 2023 AHA/ACC multisociety guideline for the management of chronic coronary disease (JACC publication).
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Same guideline as the Circulation publication; sets US positions on revascularisation and antithrombotic therapy.

title: Network Meta-Analysis of Initial Antithrombotic Regimens After Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Network meta-analysis of 41 studies comprising 12,451 patients with nonvalvular AF.
appraisal.main_limitation: Included studies are largely observational with indirect comparisons, so confounding and heterogeneity are likely.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis of initial antithrombotic regimens after left atrial appendage occlusion.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: DOAC was associated with lower all-cause mortality than VKA (OR: 0.39; 95% CI: 0.17-0.89; P = 0.03), and DAPT was associated with fewer thromboembolic events than SAPT (OR: 0.50; 95% CI: 0.29-0.88; P = 0.02).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses an area with little randomised evidence for post-LAAO antithrombotic therapy.

title: Biodegradable-Polymer or Durable-Polymer Stents in Patients at High Bleeding Risk: A Randomized, Open-Label Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label randomised trial; 1948 patients at high bleeding risk, 969 to biodegradable-polymer stents and 979 to durable-polymer stents.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label with a 1-year horizon and a composite primary outcome.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised noninferiority trial of biodegradable-polymer sirolimus-eluting stents versus durable-polymer zotarolimus-eluting stents in high bleeding risk patients with 1 month of DAPT.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 year, the primary outcome was observed in 33 of 969 patients (3.6%) versus 32 of 979 patients (3.4%) (risk difference, 0.2 percentage points; upper boundary of the 1-sided 95% CI, 1.8; P<0.0001 for noninferiority for both tests).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports stent choice with short DAPT in high bleeding risk patients.

title: Heart failure medical therapy prior to mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair: the STS/ACC Transcatheter Valve Therapy Registry.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort in the STS/ACC Transcatheter Valve Therapy Registry, 4199 patients across 449 sites, 2014 eligible for 1-year follow-up.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational, with residual confounding and survivor selection among patients eligible for follow-up.
appraisal.one_line: US registry analysis of heart failure medical therapy before mitral TEER for functional MR and its association with one-year outcomes.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Triple therapy was prescribed for 19.2%, double therapy for 38.2%, single therapy for 36.0%, and 6.5% were on no GDMT. Compared with no/single therapy, triple therapy (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.73, 95% CI .55-.97) and double therapy (aHR 0.69, 95% CI .56-.86) were associated with lower risk of 1-year mortality or HFH.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows guideline-directed therapy is seldom optimised before TEER, a quality target in a population defined by COAPT-style selection.

title: Oral Anticoagulation Use and Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion in LAAOS III.

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of a randomised trial, including 3027 patients on a vitamin K antagonist and 879 on a direct oral anticoagulant at discharge.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc subgroups by post-randomisation OAC use are not randomised.
appraisal.one_line: Analysis of oral anticoagulant use and the effect of left atrial appendage occlusion in LAAOS III.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The effect of LAA occlusion on ischemic stroke or systemic embolism was consistent after discharge across the 3 OAC groups: hazard ratios of 0.70 (95% CI, 0.51-0.96), 0.63 (95% CI, 0.43-0.94), and 0.76 (95% CI, 0.32-1.79).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports surgical LAA occlusion on top of anticoagulation and informs the interventional LAAO debate.

title: Bivalirudin Versus Heparin During PCI in NSTEMI: Individual Patient Data Meta-Analysis of Large Randomized Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient data meta-analysis; 12 155 patients randomised, 6040 to bivalirudin and 6115 to heparin.
appraisal.main_limitation: Pooled trials differ in heparin comparator use, including planned glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitors.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data meta-analysis of bivalirudin versus heparin during PCI for NSTEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Thirty-day mortality was 1.2% versus 1.1% (adjusted odds ratio, 1.24 [95% CI, 0.86-1.79]; P=0.25), and bivalirudin reduced serious bleeding (3.3% versus 5.5%; adjusted odds ratio, 0.59; 95% CI, 0.48-0.72).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs choice of procedural anticoagulant in NSTEMI.

title: Safety and Efficacy of Ticagrelor Monotherapy in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: An Individual Patient Data Meta-Analysis of TWILIGHT and TICO Randomized Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient data meta-analysis of the TWILIGHT and TICO trials, n=7529.
appraisal.main_limitation: Only two trials pooled, and the analysis is limited to patients completing 3 months of DAPT.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data meta-analysis of ticagrelor monotherapy versus ticagrelor plus aspirin after PCI in ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Between 3 and 12 months, ticagrelor monotherapy reduced BARC 3 or 5 bleeding (0.8% versus 2.1%; hazard ratio, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.24-0.56]; P<0.001) with all-cause death, myocardial infarction, or stroke not significantly different (2.4% versus 2.7%; hazard ratio, 0.91 [95% CI, 0.68-1.21]; P=0.515).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports aspirin-free strategies after ACS PCI.

title: Concomitant Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion and Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement Among Patients With Atrial Fibrillation.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 349 patients enrolled (177 TAVR + LAAO and 172 TAVR + medical therapy) at 34 US centers.
appraisal.main_limitation: Noninferiority design with limited sample size and added procedural complexity.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of concomitant LAAO with TAVR versus TAVR with medical therapy in patients with atrial fibrillation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: For the composite primary end point, TAVR + LAAO was noninferior to TAVR + medical therapy (22.7 versus 27.3 events per 100 patient-years; hazard ratio, 0.86 [95% CI, 0.60-1.22]; Pnoninferiority<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs antithrombotic strategy and device combination in TAVR patients with AF.

title: Stopping Aspirin Within 1 Month After Stenting for Ticagrelor Monotherapy in Acute Coronary Syndrome: The T-PASS Randomized Noninferiority Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 2850 patients randomised, 2823 (99.0%) completed the trial.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label trial in an East Asian population; the superiority finding needs replication.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised noninferiority trial of ticagrelor monotherapy after under 1 month of DAPT versus 12-month ticagrelor-based DAPT in ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred in 40 patients (2.8%) in the ticagrelor monotherapy group and in 73 patients (5.2%) in the 12-month DAPT group (hazard ratio, 0.54 [95% CI, 0.37-0.80]; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P=0.002 for superiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports very short DAPT with potent P2Y12 monotherapy after ACS PCI.

title: Clopidogrel vs Aspirin Monotherapy Beyond 1 Year After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 3,005 study patients, with 2,934 (97.6%) completing the 5-year follow-up.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design in a Korean population with the primary superiority comparison not met.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year randomised comparison of clopidogrel and aspirin monotherapy beyond one year after PCI in HOST-EXAM.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The clopidogrel group compared with the aspirin group was noninferior but not superior for the primary endpoint (11.75% and 13.57%, respectively; HR: 0.85; 95% CI: 0.70-1.05; Pnoninferiority < 0.001; Psuperiority = 0.13).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides long-term randomised evidence for clopidogrel as chronic monotherapy after PCI.

title: An Aspirin-Free Versus Dual Antiplatelet Strategy for Coronary Stenting: STOPDAPT-3 Randomized Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 5966 patients in the full analysis set (no-aspirin group, 2984 patients; DAPT group, 2982 patients).
appraisal.main_limitation: No bleeding reduction was shown, and there was an excess of unplanned coronary revascularisation.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of an aspirin-free versus dual antiplatelet strategy after coronary stenting (STOPDAPT-3).
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 month, the no-aspirin group was not superior to the DAPT group for the coprimary bleeding end point (4.47% and 4.71%; hazard ratio, 0.95 [95% CI, 0.75-1.20]) and was noninferior for the coprimary cardiovascular end point (4.12% and 3.69%; hazard ratio, 1.12 [95% CI, 0.87-1.45]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests omission of aspirin from the start of stenting, informing the limits of antiplatelet de-escalation.

title: Postprocedural Anticoagulation After Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: 2989 patients with STEMI randomised at 53 centres in China to low-dose postprocedural anticoagulation or placebo.
appraisal.main_limitation: Low event rate and 30-day follow-up in a Chinese population, with three different anticoagulant regimens chosen by centre.
appraisal.one_line: The RIGHT trial found that routine postprocedural anticoagulation after primary PCI did not reduce 30-day ischaemic events.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary efficacy end point occurred in 37 patients (2.5%) in both the PPA and placebo groups (hazard ratio, 1.00 [95% CI, 0.63 to 1.57]). The incidence of Bleeding Academic Research Consortium 3 to 5 bleeding did not differ between the PPA and placebo groups (8 [0.5%] vs 11 [0.7%] patients; hazard ratio, 0.74 [95% CI, 0.30 to 1.83]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses a common unproven practice and supports omitting routine anticoagulation after primary PCI.

title: Beta-Blockers after Myocardial Infarction and Preserved Ejection Fraction.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: 5020 patients with acute myocardial infarction and LVEF of at least 50% randomised in an open-label trial at 45 centres, median follow-up 3.5 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design, with 95.4% of patients from Sweden and a lower than expected event rate.
appraisal.one_line: REDUCE-AMI found no lower risk of death or new myocardial infarction with long-term beta-blockade after MI with preserved ejection fraction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary end-point event occurred in 199 of 2508 patients (7.9%) in the beta-blocker group and in 208 of 2512 patients (8.3%) in the no-beta-blocker group (hazard ratio, 0.96; 95% confidence interval, 0.79 to 1.16; P = 0.64).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Challenges routine beta-blocker use after MI in a very common population and informs guideline recommendations.

title: Ticagrelor alone versus ticagrelor plus aspirin from month 1 to month 12 after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with acute coronary syndromes (ULTIMATE-DAPT): a randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: 3400 patients randomly assigned (1700 to ticagrelor plus aspirin and 1700 to ticagrelor plus placebo) after an event-free first month of dual antiplatelet therapy.
appraisal.main_limitation: Randomisation occurred only after one event-free month of dual therapy, and the sample was drawn from a single prior trial population.
appraisal.one_line: A double-blind trial found ticagrelor alone from month 1 to month 12 after PCI for ACS caused less clinically relevant bleeding than ticagrelor plus aspirin, with similar MACCE.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Between month 1 and month 12 after percutaneous coronary intervention, clinically relevant bleeding occurred in 35 patients (2·1%) in the ticagrelor plus placebo group and in 78 patients (4·6%) in the ticagrelor plus aspirin group (hazard ratio [HR] 0·45 [95% CI 0·30 to 0·66]; p<0·0001). MACCE occurred in 61 patients (3·6%) in the ticagrelor plus placebo group and in 63 patients (3·7%) in the ticagrelor plus aspirin group (absolute difference -0·1% [95% CI -1·4% to 1·2%]; HR 0·98 [95% CI 0·69 to 1·39]; pnon-inferiority<0·0001, psuperiority=0·89).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Strong placebo-controlled support for early aspirin withdrawal after ACS PCI, relevant to guideline DAPT recommendations.

title: Effectiveness of Clopidogrel vs Alternative P2Y12 Inhibitors Based on the ABCD-GENE Score.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Genotyped PCI cohort of 4,335 patients (3,200 with scores <10 and 1,135 with scores ≥10).
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational with residual confounding and small genotype-stratified subgroups.
appraisal.one_line: Observational analysis of clopidogrel versus prasugrel or ticagrelor after PCI stratified by ABCD-GENE score and CYP2C19 genotype.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Among patients with scores <10, MAE was not different with alternative therapy vs clopidogrel (weighted HR: 0.89; 95% CI: 0.65-1.22; P = 0.475). Among CYP2C19 LOF allele carriers with scores ≥10, MAE risk appeared lower with alternative therapy (weighted HR: 0.48; 95% CI: 0.29-0.80; P = 0.004).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs genotype-guided P2Y12 inhibitor selection, where randomised results are mixed.

title: Ticagrelor monotherapy for acute coronary syndrome: an individual patient data meta-analysis of TICO and T-PASS trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient data from two randomized clinical trials including 5906 ACS patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Only two trials contribute to the primary IPD analysis, both in East Asian populations, with open-label designs.
appraisal.one_line: IPD meta-analysis of two trials in ACS finds ticagrelor monotherapy after short DAPT associated with less BARC 3 or 5 bleeding without more ischaemic events.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary ischaemic endpoint did not differ between the ticagrelor monotherapy and ticagrelor-based DAPT groups [1.9% vs. 2.5%; adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 0.79; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.56-1.13; P = .194]. The incidence of the primary bleeding endpoint was lower in the ticagrelor monotherapy group (2.4% vs. 4.5%; adjusted HR 0.54; 95% CI 0.40-0.72; P < .001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds to the evidence for P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy in ACS, a decision made frequently in practice.

title: 10-Year Mortality After ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Compared to the General Population.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort of 18,818 first-time STEMI patients matched to 94,090 individuals from the general population.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational, single-region registry.
appraisal.one_line: Danish registry comparison of long-term mortality after primary PCI for STEMI with an age- and sex-matched general population.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: STEMI was associated with a 5.9% excess mortality from 0 to 30 days (6.0% vs 0.2%; HR: 36.44; 95% CI: 30.86-43.04). In 90-day STEMI survivors, the absolute excess mortality was only 2.1 percentage points at 10-year follow-up (26.5% vs 24.5%; HR: 1.04; 95% CI: 1.01-1.08).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Locates remaining excess mortality in the first 90 days, directing research towards early care.

title: Timing of P2Y12 Inhibitor Administration in Patients With STEMI Undergoing Primary PCI.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective multicentre registry, 1,624 patients (1,033 pretreated; 591 treated in the cath lab).
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational and prone to confounding by indication, despite doubly robust weighting.
appraisal.one_line: Registry analysis of P2Y12 inhibitor pretreatment in STEMI patients transferred for primary PCI within a regional network.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Pretreatment with P2Y12 inhibitors predicted lower risk of MACE (adjusted HR: 0.53; 95% CI: 0.37-0.76), without increasing bleeding risk (adjusted HR: 0.62; 95% CI: 0.36-1.05), with a net clinical benefit adjusted HR of 0.47 (95% CI: 0.26-0.86).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses P2Y12 timing in STEMI where randomised data are limited and guidelines differ.

title: CYP2C19 Genetic Testing for Oral P2Y12 Inhibitor Therapy: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.

appraisal.design_and_n: Scientific statement; no sample size applicable.
appraisal.main_limitation: Statement based on trials and meta-analyses, with implementation requirements such as rapid results and health record integration unresolved.
appraisal.one_line: AHA scientific statement concludes that evidence supports CYP2C19 genetic testing before oral P2Y12 inhibitor prescribing in ACS or PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on P2Y12 inhibitor selection and de-escalation strategies in ACS and PCI.

title: Bleeding risk prediction after acute myocardial infarction-integrating cancer data: the updated PRECISE-DAPT cancer score.

appraisal.design_and_n: Nationally linked cohort of 216 709 STEMI patients (4569 with cancer) from MINAP and Hospital Episode Statistics.
appraisal.main_limitation: Model development in a single national dataset without external validation reported in the abstract.
appraisal.one_line: Updated PRECISE-DAPT score that adds cancer as a predictor of one-year major bleeding after STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The original score showed moderate accuracy (C-statistic .60), and the modified score showed modestly higher discrimination (C-statistics .64; hazard ratio 1.03, 95% confidence interval 1.03-1.04). According to the modified score, 94.0% of cancer patients were HBR.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Cancer is a common high-bleeding-risk feature; a better score could guide DAPT duration.

title: Antithrombotic Strategies in Atrial Fibrillation After ACS and/or PCI: A 4-Way Comparison From AUGUSTUS.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: 4,614 patients with AF and recent ACS and/or PCI, in a 2 x 2 factorial randomised trial.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc four-way comparison of a trial designed as two factorial comparisons, with an open-label VKA comparison and no estimate for the pairwise differences in the abstract.
appraisal.one_line: A four-way AUGUSTUS analysis finds apixaban without aspirin on top of a P2Y12 inhibitor had the lowest rate of death, bleeding or cardiovascular hospitalisation in AF after ACS or PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 21.9% of patients randomized to apixaban plus placebo, 27.3% randomized to apixaban plus aspirin, 28.0% randomized to VKA plus placebo, and 33.3% randomized to VKA plus aspirin.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports a P2Y12 inhibitor plus anticoagulant regimen without aspirin, a common decision in AF patients undergoing PCI.

title: Anticoagulation Alone vs Anticoagulation Plus Aspirin or DAPT Following Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort of 53,878 patients undergoing successful LAAO with the second-generation device, 2020 to 2022.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational with confounding by indication and short follow-up.
appraisal.one_line: NCDR LAAO Registry comparison of discharge antithrombotic regimens after Watchman FLX implantation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: DOAC alone had a lower rate of major adverse events and major bleeding at 45 days compared with DOAC plus aspirin (major adverse events: HR: 0.78; 95% CI: 0.68-0.91; major bleeding: HR: 0.69; 95% CI: 0.60-0.80). No differences were seen in stroke/transient ischemic attack or device-related thrombus.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs post-LAAO antithrombotic strategy, where trial evidence is limited.

title: Aspirin vs. clopidogrel monotherapy after percutaneous coronary intervention: 1-year follow-up of the STOPDAPT-3 trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: 5833 patients in the 30-day landmark analysis (aspirin group: N = 2920 and clopidogrel group: N = 2913).
appraisal.main_limitation: Landmark secondary analysis that breaks randomisation, since groups were defined by the initial dual therapy strategy.
appraisal.one_line: A STOPDAPT-3 secondary analysis found similar cardiovascular and bleeding outcomes with aspirin and clopidogrel monotherapy beyond 1 month after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The incidence rates beyond 30 days and up to 1 year were similar between the aspirin and clopidogrel groups for both cardiovascular endpoint [4.5 and 4.5 per 100 person-year, hazard ratio 1.00 (95% confidence interval .77-1.30), P = .97], and bleeding endpoint [2.0 and 1.9, hazard ratio 1.02 (95% confidence interval .69-1.52), P = .92].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Offers the first trial-based comparison of aspirin and P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy after short DAPT, relevant to choice of single antiplatelet agent.

title: Continuation versus Interruption of Oral Anticoagulation during TAVI.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: 858 patients in the modified intention-to-treat population (431 continuation, 427 interruption).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label trial with a 30-day horizon and a wide confidence interval, so thromboembolic risk of interruption is imprecisely estimated.
appraisal.one_line: POPular PAUSE TAVI found that continuing oral anticoagulation during TAVI was not noninferior to interruption and increased bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary-outcome event occurred in 71 patients (16.5%) in the continuation group and in 63 (14.8%) in the interruption group (risk difference, 1.7 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -3.1 to 6.6; P = 0.18 for noninferiority). Bleeding occurred in 134 patients (31.1%) in the continuation group and in 91 (21.3%) in the interruption group (risk difference, 9.8 percentage points; 95% CI, 3.9 to 15.6).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs periprocedural anticoagulation practice for the third of TAVI patients taking oral anticoagulants.

title: Aspirin Monotherapy vs No Antiplatelet Therapy in Stable Patients With Coronary Stents Undergoing Low-to-Intermediate Risk Noncardiac Surgery.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: 1,010 patients randomised; 926 in the modified intention-to-treat population (462 aspirin, 464 no antiplatelet).
appraisal.main_limitation: Lower than expected event rate, so the trial is underpowered to show equivalence for ischaemic events.
appraisal.one_line: ASSURE-DES found no significant difference in ischaemic or major bleeding outcomes between perioperative aspirin and no antiplatelet therapy in patients with a remote DES undergoing noncardiac surgery.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary composite outcome occurred in 3 patients (0.6%) in the aspirin monotherapy group and 4 patients (0.9%) in the no antiplatelet group (difference, -0.2 percentage points; 95% CI: -1.3 to 0.9; P > 0.99).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Challenges guideline advice to continue aspirin in stable stented patients undergoing low-to-intermediate risk surgery.

title: Edoxaban Antithrombotic Therapy for Atrial Fibrillation and Stable Coronary Artery Disease.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: 524 patients assigned to edoxaban monotherapy and 516 to dual antithrombotic therapy at 18 sites in South Korea.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label trial in a single country with a composite endpoint driven by bleeding and 12-month follow-up.
appraisal.one_line: EPIC-CAD found edoxaban monotherapy gave a lower composite of death, ischaemic events and bleeding than edoxaban plus a single antiplatelet agent in AF with stable coronary disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 12 months, a primary-outcome event had occurred in 34 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 6.8%) assigned to edoxaban monotherapy and in 79 patients (16.2%) assigned to dual antithrombotic therapy (hazard ratio, 0.44; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.30 to 0.65; P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports omitting antiplatelet therapy in AF with chronic coronary disease, a common antithrombotic decision.

title: De-escalation to ticagrelor monotherapy versus 12 months of dual antiplatelet therapy in patients with and without acute coronary syndromes: a systematic review and individual patient-level meta-analysis of randomised trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Six randomised trials; 23 256 patients in the per-protocol population and 24 407 patients in the intention-to-treat population.
appraisal.main_limitation: Trials were mostly open-label, excluded patients needing oral anticoagulation, and the mortality and sex findings come from interaction tests and are hypothesis-generating.
appraisal.one_line: Ticagrelor monotherapy after short DAPT was noninferior for MACCE and reduced BARC 3 or 5 bleeding and all-cause death in an IPD meta-analysis of six randomised trials.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Among 23 256 patients in the per-protocol population, MACCE occurred in 297 (Kaplan-Meier estimate 2·8%) with ticagrelor monotherapy and 332 (Kaplan-Meier estimate 3·2%) with DAPT (HR 0·91 [95% CI 0·78-1·07]; p=0·0039 for non-inferiority; τ2<0·0001). Among 24 407 patients in the intention-to-treat population, the risks of BARC 3 or 5 bleeding (Kaplan-Meier estimate 0·9% vs 2·1%; HR 0·43 [95% CI 0·34-0·54]; p<0·0001 for superiority; τ2=0·079) and all-cause death (Kaplan-Meier estimate 0·9% vs 1·2%; 0·76 [0·59-0·98]; p=0·034 for superiority; τ2<0·0001) were lower with ticagrelor monotherapy.
appraisal.why_it_matters: High-quality pooled evidence for DAPT de-escalation to a potent P2Y12 inhibitor, directly relevant to ESC and ACC/AHA duration recommendations.

title: Bivalirudin vs Heparin Anticoagulation in STEMI: Confirmation of the BRIGHT-4 Results.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient data meta-analysis; Six trials randomizing 15,254 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Older trials differed in bivalirudin regimen and glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitor use, and the mortality estimate for the BRIGHT-4 regimens crossed unity.
appraisal.one_line: IPD meta-analysis of six trials supports the BRIGHT-4 finding that bivalirudin with prolonged post-PCI infusion reduces cardiac mortality and major bleeding versus heparin in STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Pooled across all regimens, bivalirudin reduced 30-day all-cause mortality (2.5% vs 2.9%; adjusted OR: 0.78; 95% CI: 0.62-0.99) but increased reinfarction (adjusted OR: 1.30; 95% CI: 1.02-1.65) and stent thrombosis (adjusted OR: 1.43; 95% CI: 1.05-1.93). In the BRIGHT-4 regimens, 30-day all-cause mortality was 1.8% vs 2.9% (adjusted OR: 0.74; 95% CI: 0.48-1.12).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears directly on the choice of anticoagulant in primary PCI for STEMI and the regimen-specific effect on mortality, bleeding and stent thrombosis.

title: Derivation and Validation of the PRECISE-HBR Score to Predict Bleeding After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled derivation cohort of 29 188 patients from 4 registries and one trial; external validation in 4578 patients from MASTER DAPT and 5970 from STOPDAPT-2.
appraisal.main_limitation: Discrimination was moderate and the gain over PRECISE-DAPT was small; impact on practice has not been tested.
appraisal.one_line: Derivation and external validation of a seven-item PRECISE-HBR bleeding risk score after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: AUC for 1-year BARC 3 or 5 bleeding of 0.73 (95% CI, 0.71-0.74) at apparent validation, 0.74 (95% CI, 0.68-0.80) in MASTER DAPT, and 0.73 (95% CI, 0.66-0.79) in STOPDAPT-2.
appraisal.why_it_matters: A simple score integrating ARC-HBR criteria could standardise high bleeding risk identification for antithrombotic de-escalation decisions.

title: P2Y12 Inhibitor Pretreatment in Non-ST-Segment Elevation Acute Coronary Syndrome: The NCDR Chest Pain-MI Registry.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort of consecutive early-invasive NSTE-ACS patients; contemporary cohort of 110,148 patients, 17,509 (15.9%) with pretreatment; instrumental variable analysis.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational data with in-hospital outcomes only, and instrumental variable validity depends on operator preference being unrelated to outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: NCDR registry analysis of P2Y12 inhibitor pretreatment in NSTE-ACS found falling use, wide operator variation and no outcome difference.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Use of P2Y12 inhibitor pretreatment decreased from 24.8% in 2013Q1 to 12.4% in 2023Q1. Instrumental variable analysis demonstrated no significant differences in in-hospital all-cause death (1.5% vs 1.7%; P = 0.07), recurrent MI (0.6% vs 0.6%; P = 0.98), or major bleeding (2.7% vs 2.8%; P = 0.98) with pretreatment.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Describes real-world practice variation in a contested antithrombotic timing decision after randomised evidence.

title: 5-Year Results From the AMPLATZER Amulet Left Atrial Appendage Occluder Randomized Controlled Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomized trial extended follow-up; 1,878 patients randomized.
appraisal.main_limitation: Secondary long-term report with open-label elements.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year Amulet IDE results show similar clinical outcomes to Watchman, with more patients free of oral anticoagulation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The composite of ischemic stroke or systemic embolism (7.4% vs 7.1%; P = 0.851); major bleeding (20.1% vs 20.0%; P = 0.882); all-cause death (28.7% vs 31.1%; P = 0.217).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs choice between two left atrial appendage occluders.

title: Major Bleeding and Mortality After Revascularization of Left Main Disease.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Post hoc analysis of a randomized trial; 1,905 patients (PCI n = 948, CABG n = 957).
appraisal.main_limitation: Association from a secondary analysis, with confounding by illness severity.
appraisal.one_line: EXCEL bleeding analysis associated major bleeding with higher later mortality after left main PCI or CABG.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: MB events within 5 years were associated with a higher subsequent risk of all-cause mortality (adjusted HR: 2.71; 95% CI: 1.95-3.77; P < 0.0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Relevant to antithrombotic duration after left main PCI and to the bleeding profile of each strategy.

title: Antithrombotic Therapy to Minimize Total Events After ACS or PCI in Atrial Fibrillation: Insights From AUGUSTUS.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of a 2x2 factorial randomized trial; 4,614 randomized participants.
appraisal.main_limitation: Secondary analysis of an open-label comparison with the aspirin comparison blinded.
appraisal.one_line: AUGUSTUS total-events analysis found apixaban reduced total bleeding versus VKA and aspirin roughly doubled bleeding without a clear ischaemic benefit.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Apixaban, compared with VKA, significantly reduced the risk of total bleeding (rate ratio [RR]: 0.66; 95% CI: 0.55-0.80). Aspirin, compared with placebo, significantly increased the risk of total bleeding (RR: 2.14; 95% CI: 1.75-2.60).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Reinforces antithrombotic regimens for patients with AF after ACS or PCI.

title: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for the Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Joint Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Clinical practice guideline based on a literature search from July 2023 to April 2024.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract does not describe individual recommendations, so classes and levels must be read from the full document.
appraisal.one_line: The 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI ACS guideline replaces prior NSTE-ACS, primary PCI and DAPT duration guidance.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets United States practice and creates ESC/ACC discordance questions across ACS management, antithrombotic therapy and revascularisation.

title: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for the Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Joint Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines.

appraisal.design_and_n: Clinical practice guideline based on a literature search from July 2023 to April 2024.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract does not describe individual recommendations, so classes and levels must be read from the full document.
appraisal.one_line: The 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI ACS guideline replaces prior NSTE-ACS, primary PCI and DAPT duration guidance (Circulation publication).
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets United States practice and creates ESC/ACC discordance questions across ACS management, antithrombotic therapy and revascularisation.

title: The Australian-New Zealand spontaneous coronary artery dissection cohort study: predictors of major adverse cardiovascular events and recurrence.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre cohort of 505 core-laboratory confirmed SCAD patients (150 prospective, 355 retrospective) at 23 sites, median follow-up 21 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational with confounding by indication and a partly retrospective design; few events.
appraisal.one_line: Australian-New Zealand SCAD cohort links ticagrelor with aspirin and oral anticoagulation to higher MACE.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Oral anticoagulation on discharge [adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 3.8, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.6-9.3, P = .003] and ticagrelor combined with aspirin (aHR 1.8, 95% CI 1.04-3.2, P = .037) were independently associated with higher MACE.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds to evidence that potent antithrombotic therapy may be harmful in SCAD, where no randomised data exist.

title: Stepwise dual antiplatelet therapy de-escalation in patients after drug coated balloon angioplasty (REC-CAGEFREE II): multicentre, randomised, open label, assessor blind, non-inferiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised open-label assessor-blind non-inferiority trial; 1948 adults with ACS.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label trial in a Chinese population treated exclusively with paclitaxel-coated balloons.
appraisal.one_line: REC-CAGEFREE II found stepwise DAPT de-escalation non-inferior for ischaemic events with less major bleeding after drug-coated balloon treatment in ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 12 months, the primary endpoint occurred in 87 (8.9%) participants in the stepwise de-escalation group and 84 (8.6%) in the standard group (difference 0.36%; upper boundary of the one sided 95% CI 2.47%; Pnon-inferiority=0.013). BARC type 3 or 5 bleeding occurred in four versus 16 participants (0.4% v 1.6%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports shorter antiplatelet exposure after drug-coated balloon PCI in ACS.

title: Efficacy and safety of clopidogrel versus aspirin monotherapy in patients at high risk of subsequent cardiovascular event after percutaneous coronary intervention (SMART-CHOICE 3): a randomised, open-label, multicentre trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised open-label trial in patients at high risk of recurrent ischaemic events.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, industry-funded trial with a low event rate and a single-country population.
appraisal.one_line: Clopidogrel monotherapy reduced death, MI and stroke versus aspirin in high-risk patients after completing DAPT following PCI, without more bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Composite of death from any cause, myocardial infarction, and stroke at 3 years: 4·4% [95% CI 3·4-5·4] vs 6·6% [5·4-7·8]; hazard ratio 0·71 [95% CI 0·54-0·93]; p=0·013. Bleeding 0·97 [0·67-1·42].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on the choice of single antiplatelet agent in chronic therapy after PCI.

title: Antithrombotic drugs for acute coronary syndromes in women: sex-adjusted treatment and female representation in randomised clinical trials. A clinical consensus statement of the European Association of Percutaneous Cardiovascular Interventions (EAPCI) and the ESC Working Group on Thrombosis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Clinical consensus statement; expert opinion based on available evidence.
appraisal.main_limitation: Expert opinion, with recommendations limited by the evidence base for women.
appraisal.one_line: Clinical consensus statement on sex-specific antithrombotic therapy in ACS, bleeding mitigation and female representation in trials.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Highlights sex-specific dosing, bleeding risk and underrepresentation of women in ACS trials, a recognised evidence gap.

title: Recurrent Events Analysis of MASTER DAPT: Total Ischemic and Bleeding Events After Abbreviated vs Prolonged DAPT in HBR Patients.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Recurrent events analysis of a randomized trial; abbreviated DAPT (n = 2,295) and prolonged DAPT (n = 2,284).
appraisal.main_limitation: Secondary analysis of an open-label trial with a one-month versus prolonged DAPT design.
appraisal.one_line: MASTER DAPT recurrent-events analysis shows abbreviated DAPT had similar total net adverse and ischaemic events and fewer total bleeding events in high bleeding risk patients.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 214 NACEs occurred in 172 patients, compared with 227 NACEs in 182 patients in the prolonged DAPT arm (HR: 0.95; 95% CI: 0.78-1.16; P = 0.64). Fewer total MCBs were observed in the abbreviated DAPT group (HR: 0.78; 95% CI: 0.64-0.94; P = 0.011).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports abbreviated DAPT in high bleeding risk patients with a total-event view.

title: P2Y12 inhibitor or aspirin after percutaneous coronary intervention: individual patient data meta-analysis of randomised clinical trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual participant data meta-analysis of randomised trials; 16 117 patients in five trials.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label trials with varying agents (ticagrelor or clopidogrel) and bleeding estimates with wide intervals.
appraisal.one_line: IPD meta-analysis of five trials found P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy associated with lower MACCE than aspirin monotherapy after PCI and DAPT completion, without more major bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy was associated with a lower risk of MACCE compared with aspirin monotherapy (one stage analysis: hazard ratio 0.77 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.67 to 0.89), P<0.001), with a number needed to treat to benefit of 45.5 (95% CI 31.4 to 93.6). Major bleeding one stage analysis: hazard ratio 1.26 (0.78 to 2.04), P=0.35.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the choice of long-term single antiplatelet agent after PCI, relevant to guideline recommendations.

title: Long-Acting Factor XI Inhibition and Periprocedural Bleeding: An Analysis From AZALEA-TIMI 71.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Analysis of a randomized trial; 920 procedures in 441 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Few bleeding events and a non-significant comparison, largely in low-risk elective procedures.
appraisal.one_line: AZALEA-TIMI 71 analysis found low periprocedural bleeding with the factor XI inhibitor abelacimab, suggesting interruption may often be unnecessary.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Periprocedural major or CRNM bleeding was 1.2% of all procedures in the abelacimab arms vs 2.2% of all procedures in the rivaroxaban arm (RR [risk ratio]: 0.54; 95% CI: 0.19-1.58).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Early data on factor XI inhibition in procedural settings, relevant to antithrombotic management around interventions.

title: Sex differences in dual antiplatelet therapy de-escalation strategies after percutaneous coronary intervention: a network meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Network meta-analysis of randomized trials; 71 272 patients from 20 trials, 23.3% female.
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial-level sex subgroup data from trials not powered for sex interaction.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis suggests the effect of DAPT discontinuation differs by sex, with aspirin discontinuation ranking best in women.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: With DAPT discontinuation vs standard DAPT, a significant interaction between treatment effect and sex was found for both MACE (Pint = .028) and major bleeding (Pint = .015); MACE in females (HR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.75-0.98) and males (HR, 1.04; 95% CI 0.93-1.16).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses sex-specific tailoring of de-escalation, a population gap in DAPT trials.

title: Sex related differences in efficacy and safety of antithrombotic therapy in patients with coronary artery disease: systematic review and meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials; 33 trials enrolling 274 433 participants, of which 72 601 were women.
appraisal.main_limitation: Women made up a minority of participants and sex-stratified outcomes were not available in every trial.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of 33 trials found consistent efficacy and bleeding effects of antithrombotic intensity in women and men with coronary disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All cause death interaction hazard ratio 1.06, 95% confidence interval 0.94 to 1.19; P for interaction=0.33. Major bleeding interaction hazard ratio 0.99, 0.86 to 1.15; P for interaction=0.93.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides pooled evidence that sex does not modify the balance of antithrombotic intensity, informing guideline wording.

title: Heparin administration at first medical contact vs immediately before primary percutaneous coronary intervention: the HELP-PCI trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Investigator-initiated randomized trial at 36 centres in China; 999 patients (505 at FMC, 494 in Cath Lab).
appraisal.main_limitation: Surrogate angiographic primary endpoint and no clinical outcome difference.
appraisal.one_line: HELP-PCI found heparin at first medical contact improved spontaneous reperfusion without increasing bleeding in STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Pre-treated population at FMC showed a higher frequency of TFG-3 of IRA compared with the Cath Lab group (23.6% vs 17.6%; odds ratio, 1.44; 95% confidence interval, 1.06-1.97; P = .02). There were no significant differences in secondary endpoints, including 12-month MACCE.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses timing of anticoagulation in primary PCI.

title: Aspirin dosing after acute coronary syndrome with suspected aspirin resistance: the ANDAMAN trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective multicentre randomised trial, 2484 participants (77.2% with DM), median follow-up 18 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: The trial did not show a difference and the aspirin-resistance definition was clinical rather than laboratory-based.
appraisal.one_line: ANDAMAN found twice-daily aspirin did not reduce MACE compared with once-daily dosing after ACS in patients with diabetes or suspected aspirin resistance.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary outcome occurred in 95 of 1228 participants (7.7%) in the twice-daily aspirin group, and 110 of 1256 (8.8%) in the once-daily group (hazard ratio [HR] 0.90; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.69-1.19; P = .42).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Argues against aspirin dose intensification as a strategy in high-risk post-ACS patients.

title: Temporal modulation of antiplatelet therapy in high-risk patients undergoing complex percutaneous coronary intervention: the TAILORED-CHIP randomized clinical trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 2018 patients undergoing complex high-risk PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Strategy combined several changes at once, so the contribution of each component cannot be separated.
appraisal.one_line: TAILORED-CHIP found a tailored escalation and de-escalation antiplatelet strategy did not reduce net adverse events versus 12-month DAPT in complex high-risk PCI, with more bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary outcome event occurred in 105 patients (10.5%) assigned to tailored antiplatelet therapy and in 89 patients (8.8%) assigned to dual antiplatelet therapy [hazard ratio, 1.19; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.90-1.58; P = .21].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests de-escalation to clopidogrel monotherapy in a high-risk complex PCI population, where trial evidence is scarce.

title: Early Withdrawal of Aspirin after PCI in Acute Coronary Syndromes.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre open-label randomised trial in Brazil, 3410 patients (1712 monotherapy, 1698 DAPT).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, with monotherapy started within 4 days of admission, and stent thrombosis numerically higher with monotherapy.
appraisal.one_line: Early aspirin withdrawal with potent P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy after PCI for ACS was not shown to be noninferior to DAPT for ischaemic events but reduced bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or urgent revascularization occurred in 119 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 7.0%) in the monotherapy group and in 93 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 5.5%) in the dual antiplatelet therapy group (absolute risk difference, 1.47 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.16 to 3.10; P = 0.11 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Suggests very early aspirin withdrawal in ACS trades bleeding for possible ischaemic cost, tempering the P2Y12 monotherapy strategy.

title: Aspirin in Patients with Chronic Coronary Syndrome Receiving Oral Anticoagulation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre double-blind placebo-controlled RCT in France, 872 patients (433 aspirin, 439 placebo), median follow-up 2.2 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Early termination and modest sample size, with a total death excess that is a secondary finding.
appraisal.one_line: Adding aspirin to oral anticoagulation in high-risk chronic coronary syndrome increased deaths and bleeding, and the trial stopped early.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary efficacy outcome event occurred in 73 patients (16.9%) in the aspirin group and in 53 patients (12.1%) in the placebo group (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.53; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.07 to 2.18; P = 0.02).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Directly addresses routine aspirin co-prescription with anticoagulation in stented patients beyond six months, where guidelines rely on weak evidence.

title: Early Discontinuation of Aspirin after PCI in Low-Risk Acute Myocardial Infarction.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre open-label randomised trial at 40 European sites; 1942 randomised (961 monotherapy, 981 DAPT).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, restricted to low-risk selected patients, with few ischaemic events and a narrow noninferiority margin relative to event rates.
appraisal.one_line: In low-risk MI patients after complete revascularisation and one month of DAPT, P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy was noninferior for a net clinical composite and reduced clinically relevant bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary-outcome event occurred in 20 patients (2.1%) in the P2Y12-inhibitor monotherapy group and in 21 patients (2.2%) in the dual antiplatelet therapy group (difference, -0.09 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.39 to 1.20; P = 0.02 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports early step-down from DAPT to monotherapy after complete revascularisation in MI, a common decision.

title: Ticagrelor and Aspirin or Aspirin Alone after Coronary Surgery for Acute Coronary Syndrome.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label registry-based randomised trial at 22 Nordic centres, 2201 patients (1104 ticagrelor plus aspirin, 1097 aspirin alone).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label and not powered for individual ischaemic components.
appraisal.one_line: TACSI found adding ticagrelor to aspirin after CABG for ACS did not reduce ischaemic events and increased major bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary-outcome event occurred in 53 patients (4.8%) in the ticagrelor-plus-aspirin group and 50 (4.6%) in the aspirin-alone group (hazard ratio, 1.06; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.72 to 1.56; P = 0.77).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Argues against routine DAPT with ticagrelor after surgical revascularisation for ACS.

title: Twice-Daily Clopidogrel vs Ticagrelor to Reduce Short-Term Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events After Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: The TADCLOT Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Double-blind randomised superiority trial at a single Karachi centre, 2,201 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-centre, one-month treatment period and few events.
appraisal.one_line: TADCLOT found no significant difference in one-month MACE between ticagrelor and twice-daily clopidogrel after primary PCI for STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: MACEs occurred in 24 (2.2%) ticagrelor patients vs 32 (2.9%) in twice-daily clopidogrel patients (HR: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.44-1.27; P = 0.28).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides head-to-head data for a lower-cost option in settings where potent P2Y12 inhibitors are less accessible.

title: Personalized or Standard Duration of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: The PARTHENOPE Randomized Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial of 2,107 patients undergoing PCI (personalized 1,055, standard 1,052).
appraisal.main_limitation: Strategy bundles variable durations of 3, 6 or 24 months, and the P value is close to the threshold.
appraisal.one_line: PARTHENOPE found a risk-score-based personalised DAPT duration lowered net adverse clinical events at 24 months compared with standard 12-month DAPT.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: NACE occurred in 196 of 1,055 patients (18.6%) in the personalized DAPT group and in 232 of 1,052 patients (22.2%) in the standard DAPT group (difference, 3.54 percentage points; 95% CI: -6.99 to -0.99; P = 0.040).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests a risk-score-driven approach to DAPT duration rather than a fixed schedule.

title: Clopidogrel versus aspirin for secondary prevention of coronary artery disease: a systematic review and individual patient data meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and one-stage IPD meta-analysis of 7 randomised trials, 28 982 patients (14 507 clopidogrel; 14 475 aspirin); PROSPERO CRD42025645594.
appraisal.main_limitation: Pooled trials differ in design, with a median follow-up of 2·3 years and an extrapolated 5·5-year estimate; most trials were open-label.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data meta-analysis found clopidogrel monotherapy associated with fewer MACCE than aspirin monotherapy in established coronary artery disease, with no difference in major bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 5·5 years, MACCE occurred in 929 events (2·61 per 100 patient-years) with clopidogrel vs 1062 events (2·99 per 100 patient-years) with aspirin; hazard ratio 0·86 [95% CI 0·77-0·96]; p=0·0082.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Challenges aspirin as the default long-term single antiplatelet agent in chronic coronary disease.

title: Indications for Use of Drug-Coated Balloons in Coronary Intervention: Academic Research Consortium Position Statement.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Consensus position statement; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Consensus suggestions rest on a trial base that varies by device and setting, and the abstract gives no recommendation classes.
appraisal.one_line: Academic Research Consortium position statement classifying drug-coated balloon technologies and proposing indications for their use across lesion and clinical settings.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Offers a common framework for DCB use and trial design in coronary intervention, including in ACS and high bleeding risk.

title: Short-Term Anticoagulation Versus Dual Antiplatelet Therapy for Preventing Device Thrombosis Following Left Atrial Appendage Closure: The ANDES Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective multicentre randomised trial, 510 patients (253 DOAC, 257 DAPT); 399 had TEE at 60 days on allocated treatment.
appraisal.main_limitation: Primary analysis was per-protocol on patients with TEE, and the trial was not powered for clinical events.
appraisal.one_line: ANDES found short-term DOAC did not significantly reduce device thrombosis after LAAC versus DAPT but lowered a composite safety outcome, driven by bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary outcome occurred in 3 patients (1.5%) in the DOAC group compared with 8 patients (4.1%) in the DAPT group (difference, -2.7% [95% CI, -6.0% to 0.6%]; P=0.110).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides randomised data on post-LAAC antithrombotic therapy, an area with limited evidence.

title: Therapy for Atrial Fibrillation in Patients with Drug-Eluting Stents.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre open-label noninferiority RCT in South Korea, 960 patients (482 monotherapy, 478 combination).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, single-country trial, with the net composite driven largely by bleeding and not powered for stent thrombosis.
appraisal.one_line: ADAPT AF-DES found NOAC monotherapy noninferior and superior to NOAC plus clopidogrel for net adverse events in AF patients at least one year after drug-eluting stent implantation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary end-point event had occurred in 46 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 9.6%) in the monotherapy group and in 82 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 17.2%) in the combination-therapy group (absolute difference of -7.6 percentage points (95.2% confidence interval [CI], -11.9 to -3.3; P<0.001 for noninferiority) and a hazard ratio of 0.54 (95.2% CI, 0.37 to 0.77).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports stopping antiplatelet therapy beyond one year after stenting in patients on anticoagulation.

title: Potent P2Y12 Inhibitor Monotherapy vs DAPT After PCI in Patients With and Without STEMI: The NEO-MINDSET Substudy.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified analysis of a randomised trial, 3,410 participants (2,119 STEMI; 1,291 NSTE-ACS).
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis with a modest interaction P value, in an open-label trial.
appraisal.one_line: NEO-MINDSET substudy suggests early aspirin withdrawal increased ischaemic events in STEMI but not in NSTE-ACS, with less bleeding in both.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Among STEMI patients, an early aspirin-free strategy was associated with a higher rate of the co-primary ischemic composite outcome compared with DAPT at 1 year (8.2% vs 5.2%, respectively; HR: 1.60; 95% CI: 1.14-2.24); in NSTE-ACS 5.1% vs 6.0% (HR: 0.84; 95% CI: 0.53-1.35; P for interaction = 0.030).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Suggests presentation type should guide whether aspirin is withdrawn early after PCI for ACS.

title: Peri-operative myocardial infarction/injury after non-cardiac surgery: association between cardiologist evaluation and outcomes.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre prospective cohort; 14 294 patients screened, 1048 with PMI, 614 (58.6%) evaluated by a cardiologist.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational comparison in which availability of cardiologists, not randomisation, determined exposure; residual confounding likely.
appraisal.one_line: Multicentre prospective study associates cardiologist evaluation of perioperative MI/injury with fewer major cardiac events.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: After adjustment, cardiologist evaluation was independently associated with lower risk of major adverse cardiac events (adjusted hazard ratio .54, P = .001) and all-cause death (adjusted hazard ratio .65, P = .037) at 365 days.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Perioperative myocardial injury is common and its management is poorly evidenced, so a systems-of-care signal is useful for trial design.

title: Dual antiplatelet therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention according to bleeding risk (HOST-BR): an open-label, multicentre, randomised clinical trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label multicentre randomised trial at 50 centres in South Korea, 4897 patients (1598 high bleeding risk; 3299 non-HBR).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, single-country trial, and the abstract excerpt does not give the non-HBR stratum result.
appraisal.one_line: HOST-BR found one-month DAPT did not reach noninferiority to three-month DAPT for net adverse clinical events in high bleeding risk patients after DES.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In the HBR stratum, 1-month compared with 3-month DAPT did not reach non-inferiority for net adverse clinical events (144 [18·4%] of 798 vs 110 [14·0%] of 800 patients; hazard ratio [HR] 1·337 [95% CI 1·043-1·713]; p=0·82 for non-inferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Questions very short DAPT in high bleeding risk patients, a common guideline-supported strategy.

title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure or Anticoagulation for Atrial Fibrillation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: International randomised noninferiority trial; 3000 patients (1499 device, 1501 anticoagulation).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label device versus drug comparison with an industry sponsor and a wide noninferiority margin.
appraisal.one_line: In anticoagulation-eligible AF patients, left atrial appendage closure was noninferior to NOAC therapy for the efficacy composite and reduced non-procedure-related bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary efficacy event in 81 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 5.7%) vs 65 patients (4.8%) (difference, 0.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.8 to 2.6; P<0.001 for noninferiority); non-procedure-related bleeding hazard ratio, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.45 to 0.67.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Extends LAAO evidence to patients suitable for anticoagulation and may shift guideline positions.

title: Aspirin versus clopidogrel for chronic maintenance monotherapy after percutaneous coronary intervention: 10-year follow-up of the HOST-EXAM trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 5438 patients assigned to aspirin (n=2728) or clopidogrel (n=2710), median follow-up 10·5 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design in a Korean population, and all-cause mortality did not differ.
appraisal.one_line: Ten-year follow-up of HOST-EXAM: clopidogrel monotherapy was associated with fewer composite events than aspirin after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Kaplan-Meier estimate 25·4% for the clopidogrel group vs 28·5% for the aspirin group; hazard ratio 0·86 [95% CI 0·77-0·96]; log-rank p=0·0050.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Longest randomised follow-up supporting clopidogrel as the preferred chronic single antiplatelet agent.

title: P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy after abbreviated dual antiplatelet therapy following percutaneous coronary intervention: a meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of eleven randomised trials including 37,443 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial-level pooling with heterogeneity in populations and regimens.
appraisal.one_line: Pairwise and network meta-analysis of P2Y12 monotherapy after abbreviated DAPT: less bleeding without a difference in MACE.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: No significant differences in the risk of MACE with aspirin discontinuation at either ≤1 month (risk ratio [RR] 1.01; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.85-1.20) or 3 months (RR 0.95; 95% CI 0.67-1.36); major bleeding RR 0.46; 95% CI 0.23-0.94 for ≤1-month discontinuation.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Synthesises the abbreviated DAPT question and allows indirect comparison of discontinuation timing.

title: Extended Dual Antiplatelet Therapy for Multivessel Coronary Artery Disease.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial (DAPT-MVD); 8250 patients (4125 extended DAPT, 4125 aspirin monotherapy), median follow-up 34.3 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: Chinese population with a borderline P value and low bleeding event numbers.
appraisal.one_line: Extending DAPT by 12 months after DES in multivessel disease reduced cardiovascular death, MI or stroke compared with aspirin alone, without more bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary efficacy end-point event in 222 patients vs 266 patients (36-month Kaplan-Meier cumulative incidence, 5.8% vs. 6.8%; hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.69 to 0.98; P = 0.03).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large trial favouring extended DAPT in a defined high-risk group, contrasting with de-escalation trends.

title: 1-month versus 12-month dual antithrombotic therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with atrial fibrillation (OPTIMA-AF): a multicentre, open-label, hybrid non-inferiority and superiority, randomised, controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised trial (OPTIMA-AF); 1088 randomised, 1079 analysed (542 vs 537).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label with few efficacy events and predominantly chronic coronary syndrome.
appraisal.one_line: In AF patients undergoing PCI, 1-month dual therapy followed by DOAC monotherapy was non-inferior to 12-month dual therapy for efficacy and reduced bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary efficacy endpoint (Kaplan-Meier estimate 5·4% vs 4·3%; absolute difference 1·1 percentage points [95% CI -1·5 to 3·6]; hazard ratio [HR] 1·25 [95% CI 0·73-2·17]); primary safety endpoint 4·5% vs 8·8% (HR 0·50 [95% CI 0·30-0·81]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports short dual therapy duration in AF-PCI.

title: Dual antithrombotic therapy using potent antiplatelet inhibitors in atrial fibrillation and acute coronary syndrome: a randomized controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label randomised trial in AF and ACS terminated after enrolment of 602 patients (154 female) of an expected 1,474.
