appraisal.main_limitation: Premature termination and exploratory analyses of secondary bleeding endpoints.
appraisal.one_line: EPIDAURUS was stopped early; potent P2Y12 inhibitors with a DOAC were associated with more bleeding than clopidogrel and in-hospital aspirin, without a clear reduction in ischaemic events.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Does not support potent P2Y12 inhibitors alongside DOACs in AF with ACS.

title: Antithrombotic therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with atrial fibrillation: an individual patient data network meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: IPD network meta-analysis of six trials (10,634 patients).
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial-level heterogeneity in regimens and durations of triple therapy.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data network meta-analysis of antithrombotic regimens after PCI in AF found no efficacy difference but an early ischaemic signal with DOAC plus P2Y12 inhibitor.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 year, the risk of the primary efficacy outcome did not differ across the antithrombotic strategies (reference group: VKA plus DAPT; DOAC plus P2Y12 inhibitor: HR 1.16, 95%CI 0.97-1.41; VKA plus SAPT: 1.14, 0.85-1.54, DOAC plus DAPT: 0.99, 0.75-1.30).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Clarifies early-phase ischaemic risk with dual therapy and bleeding benefits, informing guideline wording in AF-PCI.

title: Aspirin Omission at the Time of Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in STEMI.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised noninferiority trial (PREMIUM); 2216 patients in full analysis (1109 monotherapy, 1107 DAPT).
appraisal.main_limitation: Single P2Y12 agent in a population largely from Japan, with an industry sponsor.
appraisal.one_line: Low-dose prasugrel monotherapy started before primary PCI in STEMI was not noninferior to DAPT for death, stroke or MI, though it reduced major bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Death from any cause, stroke, or myocardial infarction at 12 months in 124 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 11.0%) vs 94 patients (8.5%) (hazard ratio, 1.34; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.02 to 1.75; P = 0.40 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Cautions against omitting aspirin from the outset of primary PCI in STEMI.

title: Prasugrel versus Ticagrelor in Acute Coronary Syndromes.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry-based randomised comparison of default policies (SWITCH-SWEDEHEART); 17,095 patients (9444 ticagrelor policy, 7651 prasugrel policy).
appraisal.main_limitation: Policy-level comparison with unequal group sizes and crossover in actual treatment.
appraisal.one_line: A default prasugrel policy did not lower ischaemic events compared with a default ticagrelor policy in ACS patients undergoing PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary end-point event in 11.8% vs 11.1% (adjusted odds ratio [prasugrel vs. ticagrelor], 0.90; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.77 to 1.06); major bleeding 4.4% and 4.2% (adjusted odds ratio, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.64 to 0.99).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large pragmatic evidence on a common P2Y12 choice, relevant to ESC and ACC/AHA preference wording.

title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure Versus Oral Anticoagulation for Prevention of Stroke or Systemic Embolism in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation: An Updated Meta-Analysis of 7004 Patients Across Six Randomized Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of RCTs; 6 RCTs (n = 7004 patients).
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract does not describe trial heterogeneity or certainty of evidence.
appraisal.one_line: A meta-analysis of six randomised trials comparing left atrial appendage closure with oral anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The risk of stroke or systemic embolism (SSE) did not differ significantly between the LAAC and OAC groups (RR: 1.10 [0.87-1.39]; p = 0.42). The risk of ischemic SSE was significantly increased with LAAC (RR: 1.41 [1.07-1.85]; p = 0.02) compared with OAC.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It bears on the use of LAAC as an alternative to anticoagulation and shows a possible excess of ischaemic events.

title: Oral Anticoagulant Monotherapy vs. Combination Therapy in Chronic Coronary Syndrome Requiring Long-Term Anticoagulation: An Updated Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
journal: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of RCTs comparing OAC monotherapy with OAC plus SAPT in chronic coronary syndrome; the abstract does not give the number of trials or patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract does not state the number of trials, and heterogeneity was moderate to substantial for some outcomes (I2 = 64% for NACE).
appraisal.one_line: A meta-analysis of randomised trials found less bleeding with oral anticoagulant monotherapy than with anticoagulant plus single antiplatelet therapy in chronic coronary syndrome.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: OAC monotherapy was associated with a significantly lower risk of major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding compared with dual antithrombotic therapy (DAT) (RR: 0.50; 95% CI: 0.38-0.65; p < 0.001; I2 = 42%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Antithrombotic de-escalation in anticoagulated patients with stable coronary disease is a common decision.

title: Extended Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Versus Aspirin Monotherapy After Drug-Eluting Stent Implantation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis With GRADE Evaluation and Trial Sequential Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of RCTs; six trials involving 28,601 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial sequential analysis did not cross the monitoring boundary; substantial bleeding heterogeneity (I2 = 87%) and low certainty.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of randomised trials comparing extended DAPT with aspirin monotherapy after about 12 months of uneventful DAPT following DES.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Extended DAPT significantly reduced MI compared with aspirin monotherapy (RR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.51-0.85; P = 0.001; I2 = 37%). Clinically relevant bleeding RR, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.66-2.15; P = 0.56.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on prolonged antithrombotic therapy decisions after stenting where the ischaemia-bleeding trade-off remains contested.

title: Percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion versus oral anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation: A pragmatic meta-analysis of randomized trials within the DOAC era.
journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of randomised trials; four trials comprising 5890 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Few trials with wide confidence intervals; Mantel-Haenszel pooling with a 'pragmatic' framework and some outcomes drawn from protocol-defined datasets.
appraisal.one_line: Pragmatic meta-analysis of randomised trials comparing LAAO with oral anticoagulation in a DOAC-predominant setting found no significant difference in hard endpoints.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Overall stroke (RR 1.18, 95% CI 0.87-1.60; p = 0.28), major bleeding (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.81-1.19; p = 0.85) and all-cause mortality (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.85-1.17; p = 0.99) did not differ significantly; ischemic stroke was RR 1.36, 95% CI 0.99-1.89; p = 0.06.
appraisal.why_it_matters: LAAO versus DOAC remains contested, and the ischaemic stroke signal bears on D9 practice and on the case for further trials.

title: Impact of Stent Age on Antithrombotic Strategy for Atrial Fibrillation in Patients with Drug-eluting Stents.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified analysis of the ADAPT AF-DES trial; remote PCI group (stent age > 2 years; n = 577) and intermediate PCI group (stent age 1-2 years; n = 383).
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis; the ischaemic outcome interaction was inconsistent across modelling approaches.
appraisal.one_line: Prespecified analysis of ADAPT AF-DES testing whether stent age modifies the effect of NOAC monotherapy versus NOAC plus clopidogrel.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: No significant interaction between antithrombotic strategy and stent age was found for NACE. NOAC monotherapy was associated with less major bleeding or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding than combination therapy in both subgroups without interaction.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs antithrombotic de-escalation beyond 12 months in patients with atrial fibrillation and drug-eluting stents.

title: Dual antithrombic therapy with DOAC plus ticagrelor versus DOAC plus clopidogrel after PCI: results from the ReDUAL PCI real life registry-based randomized controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label, multicentre, registry-based randomised controlled trial within the Southeast Netherlands Heart Registry; 109 patients randomized (53 ticagrelor, 56 clopidogrel).
appraisal.main_limitation: Stopped early for slow recruitment and underpowered, so no firm conclusion is possible.
appraisal.one_line: Prematurely terminated registry-based randomised trial of DOAC plus ticagrelor versus DOAC plus clopidogrel after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Overall bleeding rates were similar between ticagrelor and clopidogrel (13.2% vs 14.3%). Major bleeding (9.4% vs 1.8%), MACCE (13.2% vs 5.4%), and NACE (20.8% vs 7.1%) occurred more frequently with ticagrelor, without statistical significance.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds randomised data to the unresolved choice of P2Y12 inhibitor alongside oral anticoagulation, and shows the feasibility limits of registry-based trials.

title: 2026 Focused Update of the Saudi Heart Association Guidelines on Best Practices in the Management of Chronic Coronary Syndromes.
journal: Journal of the Saudi Heart Association

appraisal.design_and_n: Consensus-based guideline update by a multidisciplinary expert panel; no sample size applies.
appraisal.main_limitation: Recommendations rest on expert consensus and are regional, so they add little to international evidence.
appraisal.one_line: National focused update of chronic coronary syndrome guidance from a Saudi expert panel, with new sections on ANOCA/INOCA and antiplatelet de-escalation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows how the shift to individualised DAPT duration and P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy is being adopted in national guidance.

title: Bleeding With Asundexian Versus Placebo in Patients With Noncardioembolic Ischemic Stroke or High-Risk TIA: OCEANIC-STROKE Randomized Trial

appraisal.design_and_n: Safety population analysis of a randomised trial; 12 254 participants (asundexian n=6124, placebo n=6130).
appraisal.main_limitation: Secondary bleeding analysis in a stroke population rather than an interventional cardiology population.
appraisal.one_line: Prespecified bleeding analysis of OCEANIC-STROKE showing asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy did not significantly increase major bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Major bleeding occurred in 117 (1.9%) with asundexian and 107 (1.7%) with placebo (csHR, 1.10 [95% CI, 0.85-1.44]; P =0.46). Lower gastrointestinal bleeding in 102 (1.7%) and 59 (1.0%) (csHR, 1.75 [95% CI, 1.27-2.41]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Gives bleeding data on a factor XI inhibitor given with antiplatelet therapy, relevant to future trials in coronary and structural populations.
